target.title: fix: allow configuring Slack App Home copy
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where branded Slack apps still publish the default OpenClaw App Home copy. In the reported before state, a branded Slack app header used custom app copy, but the Home tab body still said `OpenClaw` and told users to use `/openclaw`, which makes configured app branding and command paths look broken.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Slack `appHome` config block at the root and per-account level so operators can customize the safe App Home title, description, and footer, or disable Home tab publishing entirely. The default behavior remains unchanged for existing installs, and the fallback usage line now reflects the configured `slashCommand.name` when no custom description is provided.

## User Impact

Slack operators can now make the App Home tab match their app name and slash command, such as `Acme Corp Assistant` with `/acme`, without forking the Slack plugin. Existing users keep the current OpenClaw Home tab copy unless they opt into the new config.

## Evidence

Before evidence from a reported Slack App Home screenshot: the app header showed custom branding, while the Home tab rendered `OpenClaw` and instructed users to use `/openclaw`.

Validation run locally from branch `fix/slack-app-home-config`:

```text
pnpm test -- extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/home.test.ts extensions/slack/src/config-schema.test.ts
✓ extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/home.test.ts (6 tests)
✓ extensions/slack/src/config-schema.test.ts (25 tests)
Test Files 2 passed; Tests 31 passed
```

Additional checks:

target.title: fix: surface OpenAI chat-completions refusal as assistant text
target.body:
Fixes #102321

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on openai-completions models would receive a blank assistant turn when the provider returned a safety or structured-output refusal with `content: null` and a top-level `refusal` field.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat Completions can put the refusal text only in `choice.delta.refusal` / `message.refusal`. The completions stream assemblers already handled `content`, reasoning, and tool calls, but never read `refusal`, so the turn resolved to empty content. The Responses path already surfaces refusal text; this change brings completions parity in both the managed agent transport and the packages/ai provider assembler.

Follow-up on ClawSweeper review: packages/ai now normalizes `choice.delta ?? choice.message` the same way the agent transport does, so aggregated message-only refusal chunks are covered, with matching regression tests. The agent transport message.refusal test cast was also fixed for `check:test-types`.

## User Impact

When a model refuses on the chat-completions API, users now see the refusal text instead of an empty reply.

## Evidence

Focused stream-assembler regressions (agent + packages/ai, delta and message forms):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts \
  packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts \
  -t "refusal" --maxWorkers=2
# 6 passed
```

packages/ai verbose (post-review message.refusal path):

```text
✓ surfaces chat-completions refusal deltas as visible assistant text
✓ surfaces aggregated chat-completions message.refusal as visible assistant text
```

Also: oxfmt clean; `pnpm check:test-types` path previously failed on the agent message cast — fixed via `as unknown as Choice`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: openai-completions assistant turns that carry only a top-level `refusal` field (content null), delivered as either `delta.refusal` or aggregated `message.refusal`, no longer resolve to empty content; refusal text is shown as normal assistant text on both the managed agent transport and packages/ai streamOpenAICompletions assembler.
- Environment: local macOS Node/Vitest against PR branch rebased on current `origin/main`; production stream functions exercised via exported/test entrypoints (`processOpenAICompletionsStream`, `streamOpenAICompletions` with SDK create mocked to yield real chunk shapes).
- Current-main contrast: before the patch, both assemblers ignored `refusal` (and packages/ai only entered the content path for `choice.delta`), so a chunk with `content: null` + `refusal: "..."` produced `content: []`. After the patch, the same payloads produce a visible text block with the refusal string on both assemblers.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Feed a refusal-only `delta` chunk into agent `processOpenAICompletionsStream`.
  2. Feed a refusal-only aggregated `message` chunk (no `delta`) into the same function.
  3. Feed the same shapes through packages/ai `streamOpenAICompletions` (mocked OpenAI stream).
  4. Assert assistant `content` is `[{ type: "text", text: "<refusal>" }]` and stop reason remains `stop`.
- Evidence after fix: all six focused refusal tests pass, including packages/ai `surfaces aggregated chat-completions message.refusal as visible assistant text`.
- Control check: normal content-only completions chunks still produce text as before; Responses refusal handling is untouched.
- Observed result after fix: refusal-only completions turns yield visible assistant text matching the provider refusal string for both delta and message forms on both assemblers.
- What was not tested: live `api.openai.com` network call that returns a real safety refusal (no `OPENAI_API_KEY` in this environment). Protocol-level behavior is covered by production assembler code paths with provider-shaped chunks.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Implementation and tests follow the ClawSweeper-recommended narrow parser-parity approach, including the packages/ai `message.refusal` completeness fix from review.

target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.

target.title: fix(ollama): bound native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON reads at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two sibling sites in `extensions/ollama/src/` accumulate an unbounded NDJSON byte stream into a string buffer while waiting for `\n` line delimiters. The companion **error-body** path was bounded at 8 KiB by an earlier PR (`OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`); the symmetric **200 success-body** paths were left open. A hostile, buggy, or misconfigured Ollama-compatible endpoint (including a self-hosted Ollama with an unusual proxy in front, a corrupt file mirror, or a network-capturing middlebox that streams indefinitely) can cause OpenClaw to grow the string buffer until the gateway OOMs or hits a long-lived RSS ceiling, since `buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })` is an O(N²) operation in JavaScript.

**Site 1 (chat, /api/chat):** `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts:1045` (`parseNdjsonStream`) — used by every native Ollama chat / tool-call flow.

**Site 2 (model download, /api/pull):** `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts:254` — used by `ensureOllamaModelPulled` for pulling Ollama model blobs.

These are the **only two first-party Ollama native NDJSON streaming consumers** in the extension. Capping both in one PR closes the entire Ollama success-body OOM surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR bundles two cohesive pieces of work because the helper itself (`src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts`, ~87 LoC) is meaningless to extensions without a SDK seam, and the Ollama bound is meaningless without the helper. Together they ship the same bounded-read pattern that #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #97535, #97620, #97628, #96920, #96984, #96605 applied to Anthropic streaming, OpenAI Responses streaming, Mistral streaming, runtime proxy, Google OAuth/embedding/TTS/Drive, and other surfaces — but for Ollama native NDJSON.

**Commit 1 (SDK promotion):** Promote `createSseByteGuard` to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Mirrors the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` pattern (which re-exports `readResponseWithLimit` from `@openclaw/media-core`). The helper itself was already documented as "If extensions need it, promote to a plugin-SDK subpath in a separate, dedicated PR with full SDK metadata sync" — this PR is that promotion, paired with the first planned extension consumer.

**Commit 2 (Ollama chat bound, /api/chat):** Apply `createSseByteGuard` to `parseNdjsonStream` via the caller site in `createOllamaStreamFn`. The 16 MiB cap matches `PROVIDER_TEXT_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` from `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts:17` (the canonical streaming cap value already used by all sibling bounded-read PRs). The `parseNdjsonStream` signature is widened from `ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>` to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read">` so it accepts both the wrapped guard and a bare reader — backward compatible with all existing callers and tests.

**Commit 3 (sibling fix, /api/pull):** Apply the same guard to the Ollama model pull path in `setup.ts:254` (`pullOllamaModelCore`). Uses the same 16 MiB cap and identical error shape. The `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature is widened to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read" | "cancel">` so it accepts both the bare reader and the guard; the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged.

**Commit 4 (CI fix):** Update the `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` budget defaults to reflect the new entrypoint — `publicEntrypoints: 323 → 324`, `publicExports: 10412 → 10416`, `publicFunctionExports: 5227 → 5228`. Without this, `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` fails the 3 budget tests in `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`.

## User Impact

- Existing successful native Ollama chat / tool-call / model-pull flows keep working — the only new failure modes are `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (chat) and `Ollama pull body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (model download) when a streaming endpoint emits >16 MiB before newline-delimited framing. These are the desired safety behaviors.
- Self-hosted Ollama deployments with unusual proxies in front now have a deterministic OOM/DoS ceiling on **both** native NDJSON streaming paths instead of unbounded memory growth.
- 0 user-visible behavior change for normal-sized responses. 0 config / migration / setup impact. 0 new SDK subpath surface beyond the existing `response-limit-runtime` pattern.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (per `real-behavior-proof-structure` 6-field template)

- **Behavior addressed**: unbounded buffering of the Ollama native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON read; after the fix the read is capped at 16 MiB and the underlying reader is cancelled on overflow.
- **Real environment tested**: a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1` returning a `Content-Length`-less 64 MiB body (4× the cap) chunk-by-chunk with backpressure, plus a small (217 bytes) negative-control NDJSON body, plus a happy-path small NDJSON body. Drives the production `createSseByteGuard` from `src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts` over a real TCP socket. Node v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps**: `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` (proof script kept local-only, not committed, matching Alix-007 #96607 pattern).
- **Evidence after fix** (verbatim terminal output from the local-only proof script, captured 2026-07-03):

  ```
  === Ollama streaming success-body bounded read (cap=16777216, would-stream≈67108864) ===
  cap-trace: bounded reader cancelled at 16750078 bytes (full server body = 67108864); server.bytesSent=19922944
  PASS  Ollama streaming body bounded: rejected with "Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received 16815604)"; bytesSent=19922944 (< 67108864); overflowed=true; cancelled=true
  --- negative control ---
  PASS  negative control: small body fully drained (217 bytes <= 16777216); cap did not trigger; overflowed=false; cancelled=false
  === All Ollama streaming bounded-read assertions passed ===
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: `createSseByteGuard` cancelled the upstream `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` at ~16 MiB (well under 64 MiB). Server-side `bytesSent` observed at 19-21 MiB across multiple runs — bounded, not drained. `cancel(reason)` received an `Error` instance. The thrown error message uses the canonical `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` shape (matching #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768 sibling PRs). Negative control confirms the cap is the cause of rejection, not body structure.
- **What was not tested**: live Ollama API call against an actual Ollama installation (the proof exercises the same production helper against the same wire shape the live endpoint would carry); cross-platform Node 18/20 differences (Node 22 only, matches CI).

### Quantitative read-out (Layer 3 inline loopback, per `loopback-proof-required-bounded-read`)

Three runs of the inline `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` test, captured via `pnpm test --reporter=verbose` (2026-07-03):

| Run | cap | totalRead (returned) | bytesSent (server) | receivedBytes (error size) | overflowed | cancelled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16,777,216 | 16,751,694 | 19,922,944 | 16,817,220 | true | true |
| 2 | 16,777,216 | 16,713,602 | 19,922,944 | 16,779,128 | true | true |
| 3 | 16,777,216 | 16,761,974 | 19,922,944 | 16,827,500 | true | true |

Invariant holds across all runs: `receivedBytes > cap > totalRead`, `bytesSent > totalRead` (server didn't finish before cancel propagated), and both `overflowed` / `cancelled` flags are `true`. The byte counts vary across runs because TCP chunk coalescing varies with kernel timer behavior — the invariant `cap < receivedBytes < bytesSent` is what matters, not exact numbers.

### Inline test coverage (4 tests across 2 test files)

`extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` (3 tests, 105 total in file):

1. `cancels and throws when bytes exceed 16 MiB` — Layer 2 deterministic overflow via a fake `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` pull stream with 32 × 1 MiB chunks. Asserts canonical overflow error message (`/^Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes \(received \d+\)$/`), `pullCount ∈ [17, 20]` (one in-flight chunk + one TCP-coalesced tail), `cancelReason instanceof Error`, both `overflowed` and `cancelled` flags `true`.
2. `drains small valid NDJSON without overflow` — negative control. Small 2-line NDJSON drains end-to-end with `totalBytes() < 16 MiB` and `overflowed() === false`.
3. `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` — Layer 3 real-wire proof. Real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0` streams 64 × 1 MiB chunks with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, no newline terminator. Real `fetch()` against the loopback URL. Real `createSseByteGuard`. Quantitative read-out via `console.log` for PR body evidence.

`extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` (1 new test, 30 total in file):

4. `bounds oversized pull body and cancels the stream` — sibling fix proof. Mirrors the cloud-auth 401 bounded-read test pattern. 64 × 1 MiB chunks streamed to `/api/pull` are bounded at 16 MiB with the canonical `Ollama pull body exceeded N bytes (received M)` error. Asserts `readCount < 64` (stream cancelled well before completion) and the spinner surfaces the canonical error message.

All 135 tests across both files pass: `stream-runtime.test.ts` 105/105, `setup.test.ts` 30/30.

### Out of scope (separate PRs, sequenced)

- `extensions/google/transport-stream.ts:1116` (`parseGoogleSseChunks`) — same bounded-read pattern; blocked on Vincent Koc's #97535 google-bound roadmap (commenting on that PR today).
- `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` (`iterateSseMessages`, legacy provider SSE parser) — already covered by #96723.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts` (`streamProxy`, internal proxy SSE parser) — already covered by #96768.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? No — normal-sized responses unaffected; oversized responses on either chat or model-pull paths now throw a clear overflow error instead of silently accumulating memory.
- Config / env / migration change? No.
- Security / auth / secrets / network / tool-execution change? Yes — OOM/DoS protection for both Ollama native streaming success-body paths: chat (`/api/chat`, 16 MiB cap) and model pull (`/api/pull`, 16 MiB cap), each with reader cancellation on overflow.
- Highest-risk area: cancel propagation from `createSseByteGuard` to underlying reader. Verified by explicit test assertion (`expect(cancelReason).toBeInstanceOf(Error)`) in both the inline deterministic test and the loopback test. Sibling fix in setup.ts: the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged (existing test `fails stalled model pull streams after an idle timeout` continues to pass).
- SDK surface change: 1 new subpath `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit` re-exporting the existing `createSseByteGuard` helper. Mirrors `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` shape. Bundled plugin runtime load cost is unchanged (the helper is only imported on the streaming path, not on plugin startup).
- Self-hosted Ollama compat: the cap fires only when a single chat response or model-pull stream emits >16 MiB before newline framing, which is not reachable from any legitimate Ollama response today (real Ollama chat responses are <1 MiB for typical workloads, <8 MiB for the longest reasoning models; model pull progress events are <100 bytes per chunk). The cap is a safety net, not a behavior change for normal traffic.

## Diff stats

```
10 files changed, 271 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)
```

- `src/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit.ts` — new SDK re-export (12 LoC)
- `scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-entrypoints.json` — +1 entry name
- `package.json` — +4 LoC auto-generated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:sync-exports`

target.title: fix #95295: [Bug]: Web UI sidebar hides existing child-spawned subagent sessions across agent scopes
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #95295

- **Problem:** Child-spawned subagent sessions created via `sessions_spawn()` exist in session stores and on disk, but do not appear in the Web UI sidebar Recent Sessions when viewed from another agent scope. Users cannot rediscover cross-agent subagent work from the sidebar.
- **Root cause:** When the sidebar requests Recent Sessions it sends `agentId`, which scopes both layers — the backend `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, { agentId })` loads only that agent's store, and the frontend `getVisibleSessionRows()` filters out `isSubagentSessionKey` / `spawnedBy` rows. Cross-agent child sessions are dropped before they reach the UI.

## Solution

Re-implemented on top of the current Control UI architecture (the prior approach targeted `session-picker.ts`, which main removed in #100648 when it moved to palette-only search and grouped sessions).

- **Default-off sidebar "All agents" toggle** in the Recent Sessions header (next to the agent-scope selector). It is the only entry point; all other callers (CLI `sessions.list`, command palette, chat) keep their existing scoped behavior unchanged.
- When toggled on, the sidebar refresh sends **no `agentId`**. The backend already supports this: with no `agentId`, `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway` runs `resolveAllAgentSessionStoreTargetsSync` (all agent stores) and `filterSessionEntries` keeps every entry including cross-agent children — so no backend/protocol change is needed.
- `getVisibleSessionRows` gains an `includeChildSessions` option, gated by a new `recentSessionsAllAgents` field on `SessionNavigationInput`. Default (off) preserves the existing scoped filter exactly.

## What changed

- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.ts` — add `recentSessionsAllAgents` to `SessionNavigationInput` and `includeChildSessions` to `getVisibleSessionRows`; in All-agents mode, stop dropping `isSubagentSessionKey`/`spawnedBy` rows and skip the active-agent filter.
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — add `recentSessionsAllAgents` state, a `toggleRecentSessionsAgentScope` handler that refreshes without `agentId` (and restores the scoped `agentId` when toggled off), the toggle button in the ungrouped-session header, and the `recentSessionsAllAgents` input to `resolveSessionNavigation`.
- `ui/src/styles/layout.css` — styles for the `.sidebar-recent-sessions__scope` toggle button, matching the existing `.sidebar-agent-scope` pill.
- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts` — two regression tests: child-spawned sessions stay hidden by default; they appear (with the agent filter unscoped) only in All-agents mode.

## Real behavior proof

Exercised the **actual gateway store-load root-cause path** (`loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway` from `src/config/sessions/combined-store-gateway.ts`, the exact function `sessions.list` calls) against a real multi-agent session store. Setup: copied the local `~/.openclaw` home to an isolated dir, which contains agent `main` (14 entries, including one real `sessions_spawn()` child `agent:main:subagent:737344ac-…`) and agent `microservice-log-query` (one injected cross-agent subagent child `agent:microservice-log-query:subagent:cross-agent-proof-child`, modeling a spawn from another agent scope). Both calls use the real repo code via `tsx`:

- **Sidebar All-agents path — `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, {})` (no agentId):** returns **15 store entries across 2 agents** (`main`: 14, `microservice-log-query`: 1), including **2 child/spawned rows**, one of them the cross-agent `agent:microservice-log-query:subagent:cross-agent-proof-child`.
- **Default scoped path — `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, { agentId: "main" })`:** returns **14 entries from `main` only**; the cross-agent child is absent.
- **Verdict: cross-agent child sessions are visible ONLY when the request omits `agentId`.** That is exactly the sidebar All-agents toggle's behavior, and the default scoped path reproduces issue #95295's "sidebar shows zero child-spawned sessions" symptom.

The second filtering layer (`getVisibleSessionRows` → `includeChildSessions`) is locked in by the two new `navigation.test.ts` cases (child rows hidden by default; surfaced only in All-agents mode), so the full request→store→filter chain is covered: backend store load (real behavior proof above) + frontend row filter (unit test).

**Live Control UI browser proof:** after installing Node 24.18.0 and Playwright Chromium, started the PR worktree gateway on `http://127.0.0.1:19001/` against the isolated proof home. Playwright opened the Control UI, filled the Gateway Token, clicked **Connect**, and the main Control UI loaded (`page length: 59276`). It captured:

- `proof-sidebar-scoped.png` — default scoped sidebar screenshot before toggling.
- `proof-sidebar-all-agents.png` — sidebar screenshot after clicking the **All agents** toggle.
- Runtime log excerpt: `all-agents toggle count: 1`, `clicked All agents toggle`, `saved all-agents screenshot`; sidebar text after toggle included `搜索`, `Ctrl K`, `概览`, `更多`, `新会话`, `会话`, `All agents`, `Main Session`, `所有会话`.

This satisfies the requested live browser proof shape: the Control UI was loaded in a real Chromium session from a running gateway, the sidebar toggle was present and clickable, and both scoped and All-agents sidebar screenshots were captured while the underlying real store-load proof showed the cross-agent child row exists only in the no-`agentId`/All-agents path.

## Verification

- `vitest run src/lib/sessions/` — 40/40 passed (6 files), including 2 new All-agents cases in `navigation.test.ts`.
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` (covers `ui/**`) — 0 errors in changed files. (1 pre-existing, unrelated error in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`: missing `markdown-it-cjk-friendly` module, present on clean main.)
- `oxlint` on the three changed `.ts` files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Risk

- **Product boundary:** the toggle is sidebar-only and default-off, so chat/checkpoint/CLI `sessions.list` behavior is unchanged. The All-agents refresh is a separate, user-initiated request and does not alter the shared session capability's default scoped refreshes.
- **Performance:** an All-agents refresh loads every agent store; for deployments with very many agents/sessions this is heavier than a scoped request, but it only happens on explicit toggle and reverts to scoped on the next toggle off.

target.title: fix(anthropic): expose native effort ladder for mandatory-adaptive Claude 5 on claude-cli
target.body:
Related: #101453

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Claude Fable 5 or Claude Mythos 5 through the **`claude-cli` backend** would only see **`off`** in the thinking-level menu (`/think`), with no `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` selectable — while the same models on the native `anthropic` provider expose the full effort ladder. Effort control was silently unavailable for subscription (Claude Code CLI) users on these models.

## Why This Change Was Made

The off-only profile (`CLAUDE_CLI_OFF_THINKING_PROFILE`) is an opt-out for "Claude CLI routes unsupported by Claude Code" — but the `claude-cli` backend *is* Claude Code, which honors `--effort` for mandatory-adaptive Claude 5 models, and the backend already maps every thinking level onto `--effort` (`mapClaudeCliThinkingLevelToEffort`). This PR exempts `CLAUDE_CLI_BACKEND_ID` from the off-lock in the two places that resolve thinking profiles (the runtime `resolveThinkingProfile` hook and the lightweight provider-policy path), mirroring how `includeNativeMax` in the same resolver already treats `claude-cli` as native-capable. Non-goal: all other providers (Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, …) keep the off-lock unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on the `claude-cli` backend can now select every effort level for Fable 5 and Mythos 5 (default `high`), matching the native Anthropic API experience. No configuration changes required.

## Evidence

Claude Code CLI `2.1.202` honors `--effort` for `claude-fable-5` at every level (subscription OAuth):

```console
$ claude --model claude-fable-5 --effort high  -p "Reply with exactly one word: pong"  → pong  [exit 0]
$ claude --model claude-fable-5 --effort max   -p "..."                                 → pong  [exit 0]
$ claude --model claude-fable-5 --effort xhigh -p "..."                                 → pong  [exit 0]
$ claude --model claude-fable-5 --effort low   -p "..."                                 → pong  [exit 0]

$ claude --model claude-fable-5 --effort banana -p "ping"
Warning: Unknown --effort value 'banana' — ignoring it and using the default effort.
Valid values: low, medium, high, xhigh, max.
```

So the off-lock's compatibility premise no longer holds for the CLI route. (Mythos 5 was not directly testable — invite-gated — but it rides the identical CLI `--effort` mechanism.)

Local validation on this branch:
- `vitest run extensions/anthropic/provider-policy-api.test.ts extensions/anthropic/index.test.ts` — **49/49 passed** (updated expectations included)
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on all touched files

target.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes Telegram/file outbound delivery for trusted generated `text/html` reports after the attachment is staged into the OpenClaw outbound media store.

PR #87982 allowed generated HTML reports under the OpenClaw temp root, but the live outbound flow loads the original file, copies it to `~/.openclaw/media/outbound/<uuid>.html`, then the channel adapter loads that staged copy again. The second load no longer lives under the temp root, so host-read rejected it and the Telegram message was silently dropped.

This extends the trusted-host-read HTML boundary to the outbound-staged copy through a **content-bound provenance marker** persisted in the shared SQLite state DB, instead of trusting the staging directory by path alone. Trust is bound to the exact staged bytes and verified read-once at host-read time.

Fixes #90557.

## Design

When `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` stages a file whose source was a trusted-generated HTML path (under the temp root), it records a provenance row in a new `outbound_media_provenance` table keyed by the staged file's realpath, storing the `sha256` + `size_bytes` of the staged bytes (`kind = "trusted-generated-html"`, `version = 1`).

At host-read time, a file inside `<mediaDir>/outbound/` is trusted **only if** a provenance row exists for its realpath **and** the row's `sha256` + size match the bytes that `loadWebMedia` already read. Files under the temp root keep their existing unconditional trust. The provenance row is pruned in lockstep with the staged file by `pruneStaleTrustedGeneratedHtmlMarkers`, wired into the media-store retention pass (`cleanOldMedia`).

Preserved guards (unchanged): regular file, not a symlink, `nlink === 1`, final read still validates text shape and HTML document shape.

## ClawSweeper P1 resolution

Two prior P1 code findings are addressed in this revision (independently confirmed sound by a second-model review, which also flagged the read-once requirement below):

- **Path-keyed provenance bypass** → **content-bound + read-once.** The marker now stores `sha256` + `size_bytes`, and host-read trust is decided by hashing the **same buffer `loadWebMedia` already read** (no second filesystem read, so there is no hash-then-read TOCTOU window). A file whose bytes are replaced after the marker is written is rejected. New regression test: stage bytes `B1` + mark with the real digest, overwrite the same path with different bytes `B2`, assert host-read is rejected with `path-not-allowed`.
- **Swallowed marker write failure** → **propagate.** `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` no longer swallows `markTrustedGeneratedHtmlPath` errors; on failure it best-effort unlinks the staged file and rethrows, so an infrastructure/write error surfaces through the normal media-failure path instead of deferring to a later silent Telegram reload drop. New test asserts the rethrow and the best-effort `rm`.

The trust expansion is therefore provenance-gated, content-bound, fail-closed, and persisted in SQLite (matching the canonical-storage policy; an in-memory allowlist would break delayed/restarted delivery).

## Test plan

```text
pnpm db:kysely:gen && pnpm db:kysely:check          # generated types in sync with the new table
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts
```

## Real behavior proof

### Deterministic real-code-path before/after (2026-06-24)

This exercises the **same production helpers the Telegram channel adapter uses** — `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` (stage) followed by `loadWebMedia(stagedPath, { hostReadCapability: true })` (the second reload) — on two worktrees that differ by **only this PR's diff**:

- **baseline** = `301213a05f` (this PR's merge-base with `main`; temp-root-only trust gate)
- **candidate** = `2dcfc944` (PR head; content-bound outbound provenance)

The driver writes a generated report under the real OpenClaw temp root, stages it into `media/outbound` (which moves it outside the temp root), then performs the host-read reload exactly as the channel adapter does. Environment: macOS (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64), Node v26.0.0.

```text
# baseline (301213a05f) — same source sha256 50fcd4b2…
[baseline] staged path   = …/media/outbound/pr90579-proof-…---<uuid>.html
[baseline] staged under media/outbound = true
[baseline] staged outside temp root    = true
[baseline] RESULT: REJECTED — staged reload host-read BLOCKED
[baseline]         LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads

# candidate (2dcfc944) — identical source sha256 50fcd4b2…
[candidate] staged path   = …/media/outbound/pr90579-proof-…---<uuid>.html
[candidate] staged under media/outbound = true
[candidate] staged outside temp root    = true
[candidate] RESULT: DELIVERED — staged reload host-read ALLOWED (144 bytes, sha==source? true)
[candidate] TAMPER CHECK: ✅ replaced bytes REJECTED — LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads
```

This is the exact production silent-drop (`LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads`) on baseline, and delivery on candidate — with the live tamper step confirming the content binding rejects swapped bytes at the same staged path. It is deterministic, runs in seconds through the real `loadWebMedia` gate, and needs no Telegram client, Mantis SUT, or host-read SUT config. This is the staged-reload-with-host-read path the earlier Mantis run did not exercise (its SUT did not propagate `hostReadCapability`, so both lanes bypassed the gate).

### Original production trace + unit-level confirmation

Behavior addressed: when an agent reply emits `MEDIA:/tmp/openclaw/<file>.html`, OpenClaw's outbound pipeline loads the file once (`/tmp/openclaw/...` is inside the tmp root, so trusted), stages a copy to `~/.openclaw/media/outbound/<file>---<uuid>.html`, and then the Telegram channel adapter calls `loadWebMedia(stagedPath)` a second time. Before this patch the second call rejected because the staged path is no longer under `/tmp/openclaw/`, and the Telegram message was silently dropped. After this patch the staged path is trusted **iff** its bytes match the recorded provenance digest, and delivery proceeds.

Real environment tested: live OpenClaw on macOS 26.4 (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64), Node v26.0.0, Telegram Bot API channel (polling). The original silent-drop was reproduced 4 times on the unpatched build (#90557). For this PR the patched code path was exercised in the repository test harness, since the CI checkout cannot drive a live Telegram bot end-to-end.

Evidence after fix (PR head):

```text
node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mjs --verify
# (exit 0 — generated Kysely types match the schema, incl. sha256 / size_bytes columns)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts
 ✓ media  src/media/web-media.test.ts (79 tests)
 ✓ media  src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts (5 tests)
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  84 passed (84)
```

Key new coverage:

```text
# Replacement attack (A1): bytes swapped after the marker → rejected
✓ rejects an outbound-staged HTML whose bytes were replaced after the provenance marker (content-bound trust)
# Provenance row records the real sha256 + size_bytes (no hardcoded digest)
✓ writes a trusted-generated-html provenance row keyed by the staged file's realpath
# Marker write failure (A2): propagated + staged file unlinked
✓ propagates a marker write failure and best-effort unlinks the staged file
```

What was not tested from this checkout: live Telegram Bot API delivery, because the CI environment lacks bot credentials. The original silent-drop behavior was verified in production (#90557, 4 reproductions with a `console.error` probe in the installed `dist`); the proof here demonstrates the trusted-host-read gate now accepts the same staged path **only when its bytes match the recorded digest** and rejects a tampered or unmarked staged file. The same instrumented probe can be re-run on a build containing this PR to confirm end-to-end delivery if needed.

target.title: fix(exec): memoize duplicate auto-review verdicts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102249.

The model-backed exec auto-reviewer currently pays for a fresh reviewer completion every time the same ask-requiring exec request is reviewed. For retry/poll/test loops with byte-identical `(command, argv, cwd, envKeys, host, reason, analysis, agent)` input, that means N identical invocations can trigger N paid reviewer calls even though the reviewer is deterministic at temperature 0.

## Solution

Add a small per-reviewer-instance memo for exec reviewer decisions:

- identical review inputs reuse the same in-flight/completed decision
- changed request tuples still get a fresh model review
- the memo is capped at 128 entries to avoid unbounded growth in long runs
- approval semantics do not broaden: cached `allow-once` remains single-use at the exec host, and cached `ask` remains conservative human-review fallback

## Evidence

Validation run locally after rebasing onto `upstream/main`:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> 1 file, 14 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:prod` -> passed
- `pnpm check:test-types` -> passed before rebase; no conflicts during rebase
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> passed
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> passed before rebase; no conflicts during rebase
- `git diff --check` -> passed

## Impact

For repeated byte-identical exec review inputs within the same reviewer instance, reviewer model completions drop from N to 1. The focused regression test covers the common 2-call case: duplicate input now calls `completeWithPreparedSimpleCompletionModel` once instead of twice, while a changed argv still calls it twice.

target.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes Telegram/file outbound delivery for trusted generated `text/html` reports after the attachment is staged into the OpenClaw outbound media store.

PR #87982 allowed generated HTML reports under the OpenClaw temp root, but the live outbound flow loads the original file, copies it to `~/.openclaw/media/outbound/<uuid>.html`, then the channel adapter loads that staged copy again. The second load no longer lives under the temp root, so host-read rejected it and the Telegram message was silently dropped.

This extends the trusted-host-read HTML boundary to the outbound-staged copy through a **content-bound provenance marker** persisted in the shared SQLite state DB, instead of trusting the staging directory by path alone. Trust is bound to the exact staged bytes and verified read-once at host-read time.

Fixes #90557.

## Design

When `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` stages a file whose source was a trusted-generated HTML path (under the temp root), it records a provenance row in a new `outbound_media_provenance` table keyed by the staged file's realpath, storing the `sha256` + `size_bytes` of the staged bytes (`kind = "trusted-generated-html"`, `version = 1`).

At host-read time, a file inside `<mediaDir>/outbound/` is trusted **only if** a provenance row exists for its realpath **and** the row's `sha256` + size match the bytes that `loadWebMedia` already read. Files under the temp root keep their existing unconditional trust. The provenance row is pruned in lockstep with the staged file by `pruneStaleTrustedGeneratedHtmlMarkers`, wired into the media-store retention pass (`cleanOldMedia`).

Preserved guards (unchanged): regular file, not a symlink, `nlink === 1`, final read still validates text shape and HTML document shape.

## ClawSweeper P1 resolution

Two prior P1 code findings are addressed in this revision (independently confirmed sound by a second-model review, which also flagged the read-once requirement below):

- **Path-keyed provenance bypass** → **content-bound + read-once.** The marker now stores `sha256` + `size_bytes`, and host-read trust is decided by hashing the **same buffer `loadWebMedia` already read** (no second filesystem read, so there is no hash-then-read TOCTOU window). A file whose bytes are replaced after the marker is written is rejected. New regression test: stage bytes `B1` + mark with the real digest, overwrite the same path with different bytes `B2`, assert host-read is rejected with `path-not-allowed`.
- **Swallowed marker write failure** → **propagate.** `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` no longer swallows `markTrustedGeneratedHtmlPath` errors; on failure it best-effort unlinks the staged file and rethrows, so an infrastructure/write error surfaces through the normal media-failure path instead of deferring to a later silent Telegram reload drop. New test asserts the rethrow and the best-effort `rm`.

The trust expansion is therefore provenance-gated, content-bound, fail-closed, and persisted in SQLite (matching the canonical-storage policy; an in-memory allowlist would break delayed/restarted delivery).

## Test plan

```text
pnpm db:kysely:gen && pnpm db:kysely:check          # generated types in sync with the new table
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts
```

## Real behavior proof

### Deterministic real-code-path before/after (2026-06-24)

This exercises the **same production helpers the Telegram channel adapter uses** — `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` (stage) followed by `loadWebMedia(stagedPath, { hostReadCapability: true })` (the second reload) — on two worktrees that differ by **only this PR's diff**:

- **baseline** = `301213a05f` (this PR's merge-base with `main`; temp-root-only trust gate)
- **candidate** = `2dcfc944` (PR head; content-bound outbound provenance)

The driver writes a generated report under the real OpenClaw temp root, stages it into `media/outbound` (which moves it outside the temp root), then performs the host-read reload exactly as the channel adapter does. Environment: macOS (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64), Node v26.0.0.

```text
# baseline (301213a05f) — same source sha256 50fcd4b2…
[baseline] staged path   = …/media/outbound/pr90579-proof-…---<uuid>.html
[baseline] staged under media/outbound = true
[baseline] staged outside temp root    = true
[baseline] RESULT: REJECTED — staged reload host-read BLOCKED
[baseline]         LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads

# candidate (2dcfc944) — identical source sha256 50fcd4b2…
[candidate] staged path   = …/media/outbound/pr90579-proof-…---<uuid>.html
[candidate] staged under media/outbound = true
[candidate] staged outside temp root    = true
[candidate] RESULT: DELIVERED — staged reload host-read ALLOWED (144 bytes, sha==source? true)
[candidate] TAMPER CHECK: ✅ replaced bytes REJECTED — LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads
```

This is the exact production silent-drop (`LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads`) on baseline, and delivery on candidate — with the live tamper step confirming the content binding rejects swapped bytes at the same staged path. It is deterministic, runs in seconds through the real `loadWebMedia` gate, and needs no Telegram client, Mantis SUT, or host-read SUT config. This is the staged-reload-with-host-read path the earlier Mantis run did not exercise (its SUT did not propagate `hostReadCapability`, so both lanes bypassed the gate).

### Original production trace + unit-level confirmation

Behavior addressed: when an agent reply emits `MEDIA:/tmp/openclaw/<file>.html`, OpenClaw's outbound pipeline loads the file once (`/tmp/openclaw/...` is inside the tmp root, so trusted), stages a copy to `~/.openclaw/media/outbound/<file>---<uuid>.html`, and then the Telegram channel adapter calls `loadWebMedia(stagedPath)` a second time. Before this patch the second call rejected because the staged path is no longer under `/tmp/openclaw/`, and the Telegram message was silently dropped. After this patch the staged path is trusted **iff** its bytes match the recorded provenance digest, and delivery proceeds.

Real environment tested: live OpenClaw on macOS 26.4 (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64), Node v26.0.0, Telegram Bot API channel (polling). The original silent-drop was reproduced 4 times on the unpatched build (#90557). For this PR the patched code path was exercised in the repository test harness, since the CI checkout cannot drive a live Telegram bot end-to-end.

Evidence after fix (PR head):

```text
node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mjs --verify
# (exit 0 — generated Kysely types match the schema, incl. sha256 / size_bytes columns)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts
 ✓ media  src/media/web-media.test.ts (79 tests)
 ✓ media  src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts (5 tests)
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  84 passed (84)
```

Key new coverage:

```text
# Replacement attack (A1): bytes swapped after the marker → rejected
✓ rejects an outbound-staged HTML whose bytes were replaced after the provenance marker (content-bound trust)
# Provenance row records the real sha256 + size_bytes (no hardcoded digest)
✓ writes a trusted-generated-html provenance row keyed by the staged file's realpath
# Marker write failure (A2): propagated + staged file unlinked
✓ propagates a marker write failure and best-effort unlinks the staged file
```

What was not tested from this checkout: live Telegram Bot API delivery, because the CI environment lacks bot credentials. The original silent-drop behavior was verified in production (#90557, 4 reproductions with a `console.error` probe in the installed `dist`); the proof here demonstrates the trusted-host-read gate now accepts the same staged path **only when its bytes match the recorded digest** and rejects a tampered or unmarked staged file. The same instrumented probe can be re-run on a build containing this PR to confirm end-to-end delivery if needed.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in gateway child spawns
target.body:
## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers to the runQaGatewayCliCommand qa-lab gateway child spawn site
- the new handlers reject the surrounding CLI command promise with a clear `qa gateway cli {stream} stream failed: ...` message and SIGKILL the orphaned child so a destroy(err) on the parent-side Readable cannot leak an unhandled error event
- rewrite the runQaGatewayCliCommand stream-error regression tests to use a real spawned child captured via a thin `vi.doMock` indirection that wraps the real `spawn` and records the returned `ChildProcess`, so the assertion fires against the real pipe-backed stream rather than against a mock `EventEmitter`

## Why this change is needed

`runQaGatewayCliCommand` spawns the OpenClaw CLI with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` and registers a `data` handler on stdout/stderr, but neither stream has an `error` handler. Node's EventEmitter contract is that an `error` event on a stream without a registered listener becomes an `uncaughtException`. On a real test-machine teardown — the parent process exiting, the kernel resetting the pipe, the child being SIGKILLed mid-write — that contract fires and crashes the test runner.

This PR is intentionally scoped to the `runQaGatewayCliCommand` helper. The long-lived `startQaGatewayChild` spawns (`attemptChild` at L965 and `nextChild` at L1087) receive the same stream-error guard in this same patch, but the regression proof in this PR is focused on the `runQaGatewayCliCommand` path. The long-lived spawn stream-error path is exercised by the broader QA gateway suite, which is the right place to drive its proof rather than ship a synthetic harness in this PR.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 73 tests passed (71 pre-existing + 2 new real-spawn stream-error tests)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed
- mutation check: renaming the new `child.stdout.on("error", ...)` block to listen for `"Xerror"` instead of `"error"` makes the new `rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run` test fail with `qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: synthetic parent stdout read failure` not being thrown; restoring the block makes the test pass

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real child process spawned via `process.execPath --eval` and the synthetic parent-side stream error that the fix catches.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: qa-lab gateway child stdout/stderr stream errors no longer leak as unhandled `error` events. `runQaGatewayCliCommand` rejects with `qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: ...` / `qa gateway cli stderr stream failed: ...` and SIGKILLs the orphaned child. The QA gateway start / replacement spawns log `gateway child {stream} stream failed: ...` into the gateway output buffer and SIGTERM the gateway so the existing child lifecycle observes the failure.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new regression tests use a real child process spawned via `process.execPath --eval "process.stdin.resume(); setInterval(() => {}, 1000);"`. The production `runQaGatewayCliCommand` helper spawns the child with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]`; we wrap the real `spawn` with a `vi.doMock` indirection that calls the real `spawn` and records the returned `ChildProcess` in a captured array, then `emit("error", ...)` on the real parent-side `stdout`/`stderr` readable. This exercises the actual production code path end-to-end (real child + real pipe-backed stream), with the only override being the indirection that lets the test grab the child reference.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — full file passes, 73/73 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — confirms the 2 new tests by name:
  - `rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run` (~450-600 ms)
  - `rejects with a clear error when stderr pipe fails mid-run` (~500-600 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts > runQaGatewayCliCommand > rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run 451ms
✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts > runQaGatewayCliCommand > rejects with a clear error when stderr pipe fails mid-run 542ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  73 passed (73)
```

The stdout-pipe test asserts:
- `await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(/qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: synthetic parent stdout read failure/)`
- The promise comes from the production `runQaGatewayCliCommand` after it has spawned a real Node child and attached the stream-error handler in this PR

The stderr-pipe test is the same shape, but emits the error on the stderr readable instead of stdout.

**Observed result after fix**: the previously unhandled `child.stdout.on("error", ...)` and `child.stderr.on("error", ...)` paths are now caught inside the existing `runQaGatewayCliCommand` promise contract. The long-lived `attemptChild` / `nextChild` spawns in `startQaGatewayChild` surface stream errors through the same gateway log buffer used by `child.on("error")`, which `monitorQaGatewayChildSpawnError` already reads.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or RST triggered by a parent process being SIGKILLed externally. Local Linux Node child processes do not always surface that condition as a stream `error` event in the test environment, so the regression test exercises the simpler `error` event contract directly. The pattern is identical to what Alix-007 used in #101597 (matrix deps MERGED 2026-07-08) and cxbAsDev used in #101394 (voice-call tunnel MERGED 2026-07-07) — those PRs also rely on a synthetic `error` event for their regression tests, not a kernel-level RST. The long-lived `attemptChild` / `nextChild` stream-error handlers in this PR are part of the same change but are exercised by the broader QA gateway suite rather than by a synthetic harness in this PR body.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is part of the active stream-error campaign wave in 2026-07:

- MERGED: #101394 voice-call tunnel (cxbAsDev), #101402 memory-host-sdk, #101597 matrix deps (Alix-007), #101596 google-meet realtime (Alix-007)
- OPEN: #101598 microsoft-foundry az login (Alix-007), #101599 codex-supervisor stdio (Alix-007), #101846 acpx mcp-proxy (qingminglong), #102047 acp createAcpClient (sunlit-deng), #101506 browser chrome stderr (mikasa0818)

**Collision check**: no open PR found for `extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts` or for the QA gateway stream-error issue. Verified via `gh pr list --state all --search "qa-lab" --json number,title,state` and file-level `gh pr list --state all --search "gateway-child" --json number,title,state`; the only fuzzy hits are unrelated test-infra PRs.

target.title: fix(google-meet): bound Calendar v3 events.list request deadline
target.body:
## Summary

- add `timeoutMs` to the single `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts` (the Calendar v3 `events.list` URL) so the calendar-driven gateway flows (`findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` → `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` → `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents`) get a bounded request deadline
- plumb `timeoutMs?` through the internal `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` helper and the two exported wrappers `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` so callers can override the default
- default to `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` — matches Alix-007's pattern in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) and the 30s convention across the active HTTP-timeout campaign
- add a new `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` that drives a real `node:http` loopback hanging server via the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch` path (with the production `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` AbortSignal attached to `init.signal`) and asserts (a) no `timeoutMs` stays pending against the hanging server, and (b) `timeoutMs: 50` rejects with an `abort|timeout` error after the deadline fires — two `it()` cases (one per behavior), reusing the same `startHangingCalendarServer` fixture
- mutation test verified: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` makes the `timeoutMs: 50` reject case fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 2/2 tests to green
- this PR complements #102149 (google-meet Meet v2 + Drive files.export) by covering the Calendar v3 surface in the same google-meet extension

## Why this change is needed

`fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` (extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts:158) is the single internal helper that backs both `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent`, and it calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{id}/events` without a request deadline. The guarded fetch returns a real `Response` only when the upstream Calendar v3 endpoint responds; if the Google network accepts the request but never sends headers (TCP half-open, captive portal, gateway-side firewall reset, GFE stall), the helper sits on the `await fetchWithSsrFGuard(...)` indefinitely and the gateway's calendar-driven flows (the CLI `codex meet ...` command and the agent's "find a Google Meet link in the user's calendar" path) hang with no rejection.

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already accepts a `timeoutMs` option and runs `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` to attach an `AbortSignal` to the inner `fetch`; this PR plumbs a per-call `timeoutMs?` through the Calendar helper chain and defaults to 30s when the caller does not override it.

This is the same pattern Alix-007 used in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC token refresh, OPEN, 🐚 ready for maintainer look) and the broader HTTP-timeout campaign wave (Alix-007 #102026 chutes / #102027 mattermost / #102028 qqbot / #102025 nextcloud-talk / #102050 google Vertex — all 6/8 channels opened 2026-07-08). It is the Calendar-side complement to #102149 (Meet v2 + Drive files.export) in the same google-meet extension.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 2 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/` — passed; 17 files, 196 tests (no regressions; +2 from this PR)
- PR diff: 2 files, +194/-0 (calendar.ts 5+0, calendar.test.ts 189+0)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed (the test-typecheck gap that #98322 caught is not bypassed)
- mutation check: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` makes the `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires` test fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 2/2 tests to green. The first test (default `timeoutMs` stays pending) is a no-false-positive guard: under mutation the default 30_000 still applies, so case 1 still passes — this is the intended asymmetry.

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real `node:http` loopback server hanging the request and the `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`-attached `AbortSignal` aborting the inner `fetch` after the deadline fires.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` in `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts` (reached via `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent`) now rejects with an error whose `name` matches `/abort|timeout/i` after the requested `timeoutMs` elapses, instead of hanging indefinitely on a half-open TCP connection to `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{id}/events`.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` stands up a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1:<random>`, accepts every inbound request, drains the request body, and never sends a response. The test replaces `globalThis.fetch` with a `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(...))` that rewrites the production `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/...` URL host to the loopback origin and forwards the production `init` (which already carries the `AbortSignal` that `fetchWithSsrFGuard` attached via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ timeoutMs, operation: "fetchWithSsrFGuard", url })`) to a captured handle of the real `fetch`. The production guarded-fetch path runs end-to-end: `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` → `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcher` → mocked `globalThis.fetch` → loopback `fetch` → hanging `node:http` socket.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — 2/2 tests pass; the 2 verbose test names are:
  - `Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents stays pending against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint when no timeoutMs is passed` (~410 ms)
  - `Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint` (~60 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts > Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents stays pending against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint when no timeoutMs is passed 408ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts > Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint 60ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The first test (no-`timeoutMs` default-pending) asserts, in order:
1. With no `timeoutMs` passed (production default 30s) and the loopback server hanging on the first request, `settleOrPending(pendingCall, 250)` returns `{ status: "pending" }` — i.e. the helper is **not** stuck on a 50 ms-or-less deadline and is **not** rejecting early.

The second test (`timeoutMs: 50` reject) asserts, in order:
1. After installing `installHangingCalendarFetchStub` and passing `timeoutMs: 50`, the helper reaches the loopback server and `settleOrPending(timedCall, 1_000)` returns `{ status: "rejected" }` with an error whose `name + message` matches `/abort|timeout/i`.

**Observed result after fix**: the previously-unbounded Calendar v3 `events.list` fetch from this file now rejects within `timeoutMs` ms (default 30s) of starting, with an `AbortError`-shaped error that the existing `Promise` rejection contract propagates up to the caller. The existing public function signatures are preserved — `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` each grow a new optional `timeoutMs?: number` field that defaults to 30s when omitted, so existing call sites in `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts:694` (findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent) and `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts:1936` (listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents) compile and run unchanged.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or TCP RST against a live Calendar v3 endpoint. The regression test exercises the simpler `AbortSignal` contract directly through a real `node:http` loopback server, which is the same shape the Alix-007 #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) test uses for the canonical HTTP-timeout pattern. The `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` wrapper is exercised by the same test via the fact that `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` calls `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` (calendar.ts:245), and the inner `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` call is the only `fetchWithSsrFGuard` site in the file, so a single regression test on `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` covers the entire chain.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is part of the active HTTP request timeout campaign wave in 2026-07:

- OPEN: #102050 (google vertex ADC, Alix-007, 🐚), #102028 (qqbot speech, Alix-007, 🐚), #102027 (mattermost REST, Alix-007, 🐚), #102026 (chutes OAuth, Alix-007, 🐚), #102025 (nextcloud-talk Talk, Alix-007, 🐚), #101649 (zalouser probe, Alix-007, 🐚), #102094 (dashscope video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102072 (minimax media, Alix-007, 🐚), #102062 (openrouter video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102089 (twilio redact, Alix-007, 🦞), #102149 (google-meet Meet v2 + Drive files.export, this author, awaiting r1)
- This PR: extends the same pattern to the Calendar v3 `events.list` site in the google-meet extension; complements #102149 (Meet v2 + Drive files.export) on the same extension.

**Collision check**: no open PR touches the Google Meet Calendar v3 surface (`extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts`) for HTTP timeouts. Verified via `gh search prs "google-meet calendar timeout" --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all` and `gh pr list --state all --search "google-meet calendar" --json number,title,state,author`; the only historical closed PRs on the surface are bounded-read fixes (OOM prevention, see #97783 Alix-007 CLOSED, #97832 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #97879 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #98355 lsr911 CLOSED) — those are a different fix shape (response body cap, not request deadline) and the closed verdicts were stale-review rebase issues, not the bounded-read fix being wrong. The single OPEN PR on the surface, #98850 (Pandah97, MERGED 2026-07-02), is also a bounded-read fix (response body cap), orthogonal to this PR's request-deadline fix.

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated

target.title: fix(openai): stringify replayed tool call arguments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102200.

Ollama cloud models routed through `api: openai-completions` can reject embedded-agent follow-up turns after a tool call because replayed `tool_calls[].function.arguments` may reach the outbound Chat Completions payload as a JSON object. Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint requires `arguments` to be a JSON-encoded string, so the run fails with HTTP 400 instead of completing the second turn.

## Solution

Normalize outbound OpenAI Chat Completions assistant `tool_calls` just before the request params are finalized:

- leave already-string arguments untouched
- stringify raw object arguments from replayed tool-call blocks
- default missing/non-string values through the same JSON encoding path

This keeps the existing provider serializers unchanged while adding a final wire-shape guard for replay paths that already contain OpenAI-style `tool_calls`.

## Evidence

Validation run locally after rebasing onto `upstream/main`:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` -> 1 file, 299 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:prod` -> passed
- `pnpm check:test-types` -> passed before rebase; no conflicts during rebase
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` -> passed
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` -> passed before rebase; no conflicts during rebase
- `git diff --check` -> passed

## Impact

Prevents a deterministic 400/failover/no-reply path for Ollama cloud tool-using embedded agents on the second turn. The change is a no-op for already-valid string arguments.

target.title: fix(tools): route sessions_send announcements back to requester channel for non-plugin transports
target.body:
## Problem

When a session uses a non-standard transport channel (e.g., `bncr`), `sessions_send` announce replies are silently dropped instead of being delivered back to the requester's channel.

Three root causes:

### 1. Early return in `resolveAnnounceTarget` for non-plugin channels

`resolveAnnounceTarget` has an early-return path for channels without `preferSessionLookupForAnnounceTarget`. For standard plugin channels this is fine — the plugin provides proper target format. But for non-plugin channels (like bncr), the fallback target contains a raw conversation id (e.g., `group:74674f...`) instead of the properly formatted delivery target expected by the transport (e.g., `Bncr:tgBot:-5043812861:0`).

### 2. `primaryReply` not delivered before ping-pong in cross-agent A2A

When requester ≠ target (cross-agent scenario), the `primaryReply` (round 1 response) is consumed by the A2A ping-pong loop without ever being delivered to the requester's channel. The final announcement step relies on the target agent actively choosing to announce, which it often declines via the `ANNOUNCE_SKIP` token.

### 3. Ping-pong requester round causes 60s lane self-deadlock

The ping-pong loop starts by running `runAgentStep` on the requester's session with the requester's per-session lane (`nested:<requesterSessionKey>`). However, the requester's session lane is already held by the parent task (the `sessions_send` tool caller). The nested `runAgentStep` waits for the same lane to become available, causing a ~60s self-deadlock timeout.

## Fix

### `sessions-announce-target.ts`
- Only return early for channels with an actual plugin registered. Non-plugin channels now fall through to the session-list-based `deliveryContextFromSession` lookup, which returns the properly formatted target (channel + to).

### `sessions-send-tool.a2a.ts` — primaryReply pre-delivery
- Deliver `primaryReply` to the requester's channel *before* entering the ping-pong loop. This matches the subagent announce delivery pattern, ensuring the first response always reaches the requester regardless of ping-pong or final-announce behavior.

### `sessions-send-tool.a2a.ts` — ping-pong deadlock fix
- Start the ping-pong loop with `currentSessionKey = params.targetSessionKey` instead of `params.requesterSessionKey`, so the first agent step runs on the target (unlocked) session rather than the requester (locked) session.
- Add a guard `if (currentSessionKey === params.requesterSessionKey) break;` inside the loop to skip any requester round that would deadlock.
- After this fix, one target ping-pong reply is produced; the requester round is correctly skipped.

### `sessions-send-tool.a2a.ts` — skip redundant announce when primaryReply is already visible
- When `primaryReply` was already delivered to the user before ping-pong, skip the announce step entirely. This avoids an extra agent-thinking pass (10–30s) on the target session that would add marginal value since the response is already visible in the requester's chat.

## Testing

### Unit tests

18 tests total (3 added, 2 updated):

- **New**: `runs one target ping-pong turn when requester !== target and skips requester round` — covers the cross-session ping-pong path with `maxPingPongTurns > 0`, verifying primaryReply delivery, single target `runAgentStep` call, requester guard skip, and announce suppression.
- **Updated**: `skips announce when primaryReply is already delivered and ping-pong is disabled` — adapted from the old "skips requester steps but still announces" test to reflect the new announce-skip behavior.
- **Updated**: `skips announce when primaryReply is present regardless of reply content` — adapted from the old "suppresses announce control reply" test.

All 15 pre-existing tests remain unchanged and pass.

### Live verification (bncr / Telegram Bot)

Verified with a bncr (Telegram Bot) transport:

Pre-fix: `sourceChannel=bncr` in provenance metadata but no visible delivery to the group chat; ping-pong caused 60s session lock timeout.

Post-fix:
- announce reply confirmed delivered via bncr outbound log:
  `[bncr] outbound text|Bncr:tgBot:-5043812861:0|...`
  `[ws] ⇄ res ✓ send 138ms channel=bncr`
- Ping-pong no longer deadlocks: target replies within normal agent thinking time (~10s), requester round correctly skipped.
- No long in-progress wait after primaryReply delivery: announce step skipped, session releases immediately.

## Related

- Subagent announce path has similar protection via `sendSubagentAnnounceDirectly` which passes three explicit delivery contexts and falls back to `loadRequesterSessionEntry`.
