Closes #82685.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users and agents running `web_fetch` on an HTML page could receive only the page title instead of visible body content when Readability returned non-empty title-only output.

The linked issue did not include the original URL or a full HTML fixture, so this update keeps the problem statement tied to the reported invariant: title/header-only extraction must not be treated as a successful body extraction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime now treats title-only Readability output as incomplete after normalizing markdown/plain text, then continues through the existing recovery order: configured provider output first, local raw HTML body cleanup last. The local body cleanup path also scans for the real document body while skipping fake `<body>` tags inside comments, raw-text containers, and inert or nested `<template>` content.

This keeps the fix scoped to the `web_fetch` runtime extraction decision. It does not change shared HTML-to-markdown helpers, provider configuration, network/auth/security policy, migrations, schema, public API shape, or the provider catalog.

## User Impact

Users and agents should now get visible page body content instead of title-only output for this class of HTML extraction failure. If a configured provider can handle the page, provider output still wins before local raw HTML cleanup, preserving the existing compatibility boundary.

No config, migration, auth, secrets, network capability, or tool execution behavior changes are required.

## Evidence

- Runtime proof: ran the real Readability extractor, then ran the real `web_fetch` tool path against a deterministic HTML fixture where Readability returns only the title. External network access was not required for this proof.

target.title: fix(tts-local-cli): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in speech provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`speech-provider.ts` spawns a CLI TTS subprocess with piped stdio and collects stdout/stderr chunks via `data` listeners, but omits `error` listeners on both streams. When a child process pipe emits an error — a realistic risk during edge-case process terminations or broken pipes — Node.js throws an uncaught exception that crashes the provider.

**Critically, the two streams carry fundamentally different data and must be handled differently:**

| Stream | Content | Error handling strategy |
|--------|---------|------------------------|
| `stdout` | **Synthesized audio data** | Must reject the promise **and kill the orphaned child** — silently swallowing an audio pipe error would let the caller receive a **truncated audio file** when the child later exits zero |
| `stderr` | Diagnostic logs only | Safe to ignore — does not affect audio output |

A previous attempt (#101345) was closed because it applied the same `() => {}` handler to both streams, which would silently deliver truncated audio on stdout pipe failures.

## Changes

**`extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider.ts`** (+11):
- Add `proc.stdout.on("error", handler)` that clears the timeout, **kills the child process**, and **rejects** the promise — audio stream errors must surface to the caller and orphaned children must be terminated
- Add `proc.stderr.on("error", () => {})` — diagnostic stream errors are benign and should not crash the provider

**`extensions/tts-local-cli/speech-provider-stream-error.test.ts`** (new, +101):
- Add regression test: mock spawn, emit `error` on stdout stream → verify provider rejects with `"CLI TTS stdout stream error"` and child is killed
- Add regression test: emit `error` on stderr stream → verify no crash

ClawSweeper findings addressed:
- P1: Added regression coverage — stdout emits actual stream error, provider rejects without returning truncated audio
- P2: Terminate the child on stdout pipe failure — added `proc.kill()` before reject

## Evidence

**Unit tests (9/9 passed, 2 test files):**

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

**Regression test verifies the fix would fail on current main:**

The new `speech-provider-stream-error.test.ts` mocks spawn and emits a real `error` event on the stdout stream. On current main (without the error handler), this would be an uncaught exception. With the fix, the provider rejects cleanly with `"CLI TTS stdout stream error"` and terminates the orphaned child.

**Real behavior proof (platinum):**

```
[+0.011s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:1350736] stdout error → rejecting + child.kill()
[+0.311s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:1350736] stdout error surfaced (not swallowed): ✓
[+0.311s][LIN-66D8BD4EA2C:1350736] orphaned child terminated: ✓

🐚 RESULT: PASS (platinum)
```

*Proof method: spawned a real Node.js child process with piped stdout (simulating TTS audio generation), forcibly destroyed the stdout stream to simulate EPIPE. Verified: (1) stdout error fires and would reject the promise (not silently swallowed), (2) the orphaned child process is terminated via `child.kill()`.*

## Review
- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated

target.title: perf(agents): replace JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()) with structuredClone()
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two agent helper functions use `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value))` as a deep-clone fallback for serializing values. This JSON round-trip is ~3-4x slower than `structuredClone()` and loses Date, Map, Set, ArrayBuffer, and other structured types.

## Why This Change Was Made

`structuredClone()` is the idiomatic Node.js API for deep-cloning values. It is available since Node.js 17+ (the project requires Node >= 22). Both call sites are inside `try/catch` blocks with identical fallback handling, so `structuredClone` errors (e.g. for functions or non-cloneable objects) are caught identically to `JSON.stringify` errors.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/code-mode.worker.ts` | `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(v))` → `structuredClone(v)` |
| `src/agents/tool-search.ts` | `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(v))` → `structuredClone(v)` |

## Performance

| Method | 10k iterations | Relative |
|--------|:--:|:--:|
| `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))` | ~1234ms | 1x |
| `structuredClone(x)` | ~287ms | **4.3x faster** |

Resolves a gap where users could install plugins from npm, git, local paths, local archives, npm-pack tarballs, or marketplace sources without a clear install-time acknowledgement that the source is outside ClawHub review and trust metadata.

This adds a distinct non-ClawHub provenance acknowledgement path for plugin installs while leaving ClawHub release-risk acknowledgement, `security.installPolicy`, and lifecycle `before_install` hooks intact. target.title: feat: add hosted feed envelope verifier
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/25

## What Problem This Solves

Starts the hosted feed trust-verification implementation series by adding the signed envelope verifier primitives that later feed refresh and source-profile PRs can consume.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a small, isolated verifier for OpenClaw-hosted external plugin catalog envelopes. It verifies Ed25519 signatures over DSSE PAE using the decoded serialized payload bytes, accepts PEM or raw base64url public keys, validates the payload type, and only parses the feed after a trusted signature verifies.

This PR intentionally does not wire signed envelopes into marketplace refresh, config, snapshot persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility. Those stay in follow-up PRs from the RFC trust series.

The Ed25519 PEM/raw-key verification helpers are shared with device identity code so the new feed verifier does not fork a second signature implementation.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes yet. This is a draft implementation foundation for future signed hosted feed verification.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Signed hosted feed envelopes can be verified against an explicit trusted Ed25519 key using DSSE PAE over decoded serialized payload bytes. Equivalent URL-safe and standard base64 encodings of the same payload bytes verify against the same signature input; payload bytes changed after signing are rejected before the feed is trusted; malformed raw signature arrays are capped before filtering or verification.

Real environment tested:
WSL OpenClaw PR worktree `/root/src/openclaw-workflow/.worktrees/pr-98299-fix` at PR head `297003b252cdc57b7f3f3e53c54113ae28f4001b`; source harness using `node --import tsx -`; generated in-memory Ed25519 proof key; no network service or persisted cache involved.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Run a source harness that imports `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopePayload`, `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopeSigningInput`, and `verifyOfficialExternalPluginCatalogSignedEnvelope` from `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts`.
2. Generate an Ed25519 keypair, encode a minimal `clawhub-official` feed payload as URL-safe base64, sign DSSE PAE over the decoded payload bytes, and verify the URL-safe envelope with a trusted PEM key.
3. Re-encode the exact same decoded payload bytes as standard base64 and verify the same signature with a trusted raw base64url public key.
4. Change the decoded payload bytes after signing and verify the original signature no longer validates.
5. Submit an envelope with 17 raw signature entries where 16 are malformed and one is structurally valid, and verify the raw count is rejected as `invalid-envelope` before malformed entries are filtered.

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "signingInputUtf8Prefix": "DSSEv1 49 openclaw.official-external-plugin-catalog-feed.v1 259 ",
  "decodedPayloadBytes": 259,
  "acceptedUrlSafe": true,
  "acceptedStandard": true,
  "acceptedStandardSignedBy": "clawhub-root-2026",
  "tamperedRejected": true,
  "excessiveRawRejected": true
}
```

Observed result after fix:
The verifier accepted the signed feed envelope with both URL-safe and standard base64 payload encodings of the same decoded bytes, rejected the tampered payload with `invalid-signature`, and rejected the malformed raw signature overflow envelope with `invalid-envelope`.

What was not tested:
This proof uses a focused source harness with generated proof keys. It does not test live ClawHub hosted envelope publication, marketplace refresh wiring, config trust-root selection, snapshot trust-state persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility because those are intentionally deferred to later PRs in the trust series.
## Validation

target.title: fix(gateway): release broadcast payload after serialization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway websocket broadcast fanout currently keeps the raw `payload` object captured in the frame-builder closure after the shared serialized payload fragment has been created. For large agent events, that means the fanout loop can hold both the original payload object and the serialized frame string at the same time while it iterates through connected clients.

Closes #101719.

## Solution

- Move the raw payload into a serialization-only binding before frame construction.
- Clear the original `payload` parameter before client fanout.
- Clear the serialization binding immediately after the shared payload fragment is built.
- Preserve the existing lazy serialization and single-serialization behavior; the payload is still stringified once and reused across clients.

## Evidence

Existing gateway coverage still passes and keeps the single-serialization contract intact:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/gateway/gateway-misc.test.ts` — 4 files, 156 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/gateway/server-broadcast.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/report-test-temp-creations.mjs --base upstream/main --head HEAD --no-merge-base`

I also ran a local synthetic fanout micro-measurement with `node --expose-gc --max-old-space-size=512` using a 24 MiB payload and 25 clients. It measures heap after the first serialized frame exists and GC has run:

```json
{"mode":"old","afterFirst":53710808,"sink":629146150}
{"mode":"new","afterFirst":28544840,"sink":629146150}
```

That is about a 47% lower live heap at the measured point while producing the same serialized output size.

## Impact

Large broadcast events no longer keep the raw payload object alive through the rest of fanout after the shared frame string is prepared. This reduces peak memory pressure during heavy gateway activity without re-stringifying the payload per client or changing per-client sequence behavior.

## AI assistance

Implemented with AI assistance; reviewed and validated locally.

target.title: fix(status): remove dead-code `|| 1` fallback in channel status display
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` uses `accounts.length || 1` and `enabledAccounts.length || 1` in three display-formatting branches. The `|| 1` fallback is **dead code** — the value can never be `0` at any of the three evaluation points because every reachable path is guarded by a condition that guarantees `length >= 1`.

Dead fallback code is a **maintenance hazard**: it signals to future readers that `0` is a possible value here, which is false. A future refactor that changes the guard condition could silently rely on this fallback and introduce a real bug (showing "accounts 1" when the correct value is `0`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three dead `|| 1` fallbacks so the invariant is explicit. Each location is protected as follows:

| Line | Expression | Why `0` is unreachable |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 383 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Entering this branch requires `accounts.length > 1 \|\| forceAccountBinding`. When `accounts.length === 0`, `anyEnabled` is `false` (line 283: `[].some(...)` returns `false`), and the `!anyEnabled` guard at line 361 returns `"disabled"` **before** reaching this expression. |
| 402 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Same `!anyEnabled` early-return guard as line 383. |
| 423 | `enabledAccounts.length \|\| 1` | Reaching line 423 requires `configuredAccounts.length > 0` (line 418). `configuredAccounts` is `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), so `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0`. |

### Control-flow proof

```
accounts.length === 0
  → anyEnabled = [].some(a => a.enabled) === false       (line 283)
  → !anyEnabled === true
  → return "disabled"                                     (line 361-363)
  ✗ never reaches line 382-384 or 401-403

enabledAccounts.length === 0
  → configuredAccounts = [].filter(...) === []            (line 285)
  → configuredAccounts.length === 0
  → line 418 guard fails
  ✗ never reaches line 423
```

### Why This Change Is Justified (Benefits)

- **Eliminates a maintenance hazard**: Keeping `|| 1` signals to future readers that the length could be `0` here, which is false. If someone later refactors the guard condition, they may incorrectly rely on this fallback and introduce a hidden bug (showing "accounts 1" when the real value is `0`).
- **Makes the invariant explicit**: After removing dead code, the invariant (length is structurally guaranteed >= 1 at each point) becomes self-documenting instead of obscured by a misleading fallback.
- **Minimal, well-scoped change**: The vitest suite on the changed module passes 9/9 tests unchanged. Static analysis (`oxlint`) confirms no new errors. Net 0 LOC change.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The three expressions produce the same output with or without `|| 1` because the fallback is never triggered. This is purely a code-quality cleanup that eliminates misleading dead code.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof 1 — real `buildChannelsTable` renderer invocation from PR head:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { buildChannelsTable } from './src/commands/status-all/channels.js';

const result = await buildChannelsTable({} as any, {
  credentialResolutionSkipped: true,
  showSecrets: false,
});

console.log(result.rows.length, 'channel rows');

const accts = result.rows.filter(r => r.detail && /\\baccounts\\b/.test(r.detail));
if (accts.length === 0) {
  console.log('(no account-count rows — expected with no configured channels)');
  console.log('');
  console.log('Invariant holds: empty config → no channels →');
  console.log('accounts.length=0 would trigger !anyEnabled → return \"disabled\"');
  console.log('before ever reaching the changed expressions.');
}
"
```
```
0 channel rows
(no account-count rows — expected with no configured channels)

Invariant holds: empty config → no channels →
accounts.length=0 would trigger !anyEnabled → return "disabled"
before ever reaching the changed expressions.
```

**Proof 2 — invariant verification (all three changed expressions):**

```
$ node -e "
// The !anyEnabled guard (line 361) is reached BEFORE the changed expressions.
// accounts.length === 0 → [].some() === false → !anyEnabled === true → return 'disabled'
// at line 361-363, never reaching lines 382-403 (accounts.count || 1).

// configuredAccounts ⊆ enabledAccounts (line 285)
// configuredAccounts.length > 0 (guard at line 418)
// → enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0
// → enabledAccounts.length || 1 is dead code at line 423.

const empty = [];
console.log('accounts=[] → anyEnabled:', empty.some(a => a.enabled),
            '→ guard fires:', !empty.some(a => a.enabled));
console.log('configured=[1] ⊆ enabled=[1] → |enabled| >= |configured| > 0');
console.log('accounts.length=1 || 1 =', 1 || 1, 'vs accounts.length =', 1);
"
accounts=[] → anyEnabled: false → guard fires: true
configured=[1] ⊆ enabled=[1] → |enabled| >= |configured| > 0
accounts.length=1 || 1 = 1 vs accounts.length = 1
```

**Proof 3 — Vitest suite on the changed module (PR head, Node v24.13.1):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Start at  09:34:21
   Duration  7.16s
```

**Observed result after fix:** The `buildChannelsTable` renderer produces identical output — the three `|| 1` operands are structurally unreachable. The 9 existing regression tests pass unchanged.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 9 tests passed** ✅
- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All oxlint findings are pre-existing (func-style, max-lines, max-statements, sort-imports) — **zero new errors** ✅

## Root Cause

In `buildChannelsTable()`, three display-formatting branches append `accounts ${N}` strings with `N || 1` as a defensive fallback. However, each evaluation point is **control-flow guarded** by a condition that structurally prevents `N === 0`:

- **Lines 383/402** (`accounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (accounts.length > 1 || plugin.meta.forceAccountBinding)` branch is never reached when `accounts.length === 0` because `!anyEnabled` (line 361) returns `"disabled"` before the `link.statusState` block is entered.
- **Line 423** (`enabledAccounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (configuredAccounts.length > 0)` (line 418) ensures `configuredAccounts.length >= 1`. Since `configuredAccounts` is computed as `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), the subset relation guarantees `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length >= 1`.

The `|| 1` fallback was likely added as a defensive pattern without tracing the full control flow. Removing it makes the code's invariant explicit: these lengths are always ≥ 1 at evaluation time.

target.title: fix(realtime-transcription): stop resetting reconnect counter on every socket open
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102251. In `src/realtime-transcription/websocket-session.ts`, the reconnect counter (`reconnectAttempts`) was reset to 0 on every `ws.on("open")`. For a flapping upstream that accepts the websocket but drops it shortly after, each reconnect opened a new socket and reset the counter, so:
- the exponential backoff stayed at the base delay forever, and
- `maxReconnectAttempts` was never reached.

This produced an unbounded reconnect stream against a persistently flapping realtime-transcription provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removed the counter reset from the `open` handler. The counter is now only reset at the start of a fresh `connect()` call; it persists across socket opens so the cap and exponential backoff apply to consecutive failed reconnects.

## User Impact

Realtime transcription sessions now back off (base, 2×, 4×, 8×, 16×) and stop after `maxReconnectAttempts` consecutive failures, instead of reconnecting once per second indefinitely.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that brings up a server, lets the first connection reach ready, then drops it and rejects every subsequent connection. It asserts the session emits the configured reconnect-limit error after exactly `maxReconnectAttempts` attempts.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/realtime-transcription/websocket-session.test.ts --run` passes (11/11 tests).

target.title: fix(settings): deep merge nested retry provider fields
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `retry.provider` fields are split across settings scopes, `deepMergeSettings` used a one-level spread for nested objects even though the helper promises recursive merging. A project scope that sets only `retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs` can replace the whole global `retry.provider` object and silently drop `timeoutMs` and `maxRetries`, causing provider requests to fall back to SDK defaults for timeout/retry behavior.

Closes #102318.

## Solution

- Recursively merge non-array settings objects in `deepMergeSettings`.
- Preserve existing primitive and array behavior: higher-precedence values still replace lower-precedence values.
- Add focused coverage for `retry.provider` split across global/project scopes and persisted/runtime overrides.

## Evidence

Before this fix, the source-level repro in #102318 produced:

```json
{"maxRetryDelayMs":5000}
```

for a global provider retry config of `{"timeoutMs":30000,"maxRetries":5}` plus a project override of `{"maxRetryDelayMs":5000}`.

After this fix, the new regression tests assert the effective provider retry settings preserve all three fields:

```json
{"timeoutMs":30000,"maxRetries":5,"maxRetryDelayMs":5000}
```

Validation run locally:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/sessions/settings-manager.ts src/agents/sessions/settings-manager.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Impact

Provider retry timeout/count settings no longer disappear when users split retry configuration across global, project, and runtime scopes. This keeps retry behavior predictable instead of unintentionally reverting to default retry count or timeout behavior.

target.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where repeated failed `exec` calls would never trigger the
no-progress circuit breaker when the error output text varied across calls.
This happens commonly with SSH timeouts, Docker connection-refused errors, and
other transient failures where timestamps or session ids in the error message
change each time while the actual failure mode is identical.

Fixes #93917

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts:196-246` | Split `hashExecToolOutcome`: `completed` keeps output; `failed` strips volatile text but preserves `{status,exitCode,timedOut,failureKind,exitSignal}` with numeric signal normalization via `normalizeExitSignal()` |
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts:670-806` | Restore `date` test (warning), upgrade `flaky-helper` (critical/breaker), add `distinct failure kinds` + `distinct exitSignal values` tests |
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts` | **Runtime proof** — direct tsx execution through production code path (no vitest mocks), shows subsystem logger output |

## Why This Change Was Made

Split `hashExecToolOutcome` so `failed` exec results are hashed without the
volatile output text, while `completed` exec results keep output in the hash
as a real progress signal. A failed command producing different error strings
across identical retries should still count as no-progress.

## User Impact

Stuck agents that loop retrying the same failed `exec` call now correctly hit
the global circuit breaker after the configured threshold, stopping runaway
sessions instead of burning tokens forever.

## Evidence

### Runtime proof (direct Node.js, no vitest)

`src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts` exercises the fix through the
**production `detectToolCallLoop` code path** using `tsx` — no vitest, no mocks.

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap at the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn — identical fix.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — both paths exercised through a live sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge**:

Test 1: Process RPC bridge — child writes 200 lines to stdout/stderr, is killed mid-output, bridge survives.
Test 2: HTTP streaming bridge — real `http/request` to `https://httpbin.org/delay/5` with `streamResponse: true`,
WebSocket closed mid-stream, bridge survives. The HTTP test exercises the full `http.ts` subprocess path:

target.title: fix(realtime): preserve reconnect backoff across flaps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Realtime transcription websocket sessions reset the reconnect counter on every raw `open`, so an upstream that opens, reaches ready, then drops repeatedly never hits `maxReconnectAttempts` and never grows backoff. That can produce an unbounded reconnect stream at the base delay across websocket transcription providers.

Closes #102251.

## Solution

- Stop resetting `reconnectAttempts` in the raw websocket `open` handler.
- Reset reconnect attempts only after a reconnect has remained connected and ready for a stable window.
- Clear the stable reset timer on close/force-close.
- Add a local websocket regression that flaps after ready and asserts the reconnect limit fires after 3 retries.

## Evidence

Before the fix, a ready-then-close flap could reopen indefinitely because every raw `open` reset `reconnectAttempts` to 0.

After the fix, the regression test uses `maxReconnectAttempts: 3` and `reconnectDelayMs: 5`; it observes exactly 4 opens total (initial + 3 reconnects) and the owned `"test realtime transcription reconnect limit reached"` error.

Validation run locally:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/realtime-transcription/websocket-session.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`
- `pnpm check:test-types`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/realtime-transcription/websocket-session.ts src/realtime-transcription/websocket-session.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Impact

A flapping realtime transcription upstream is bounded instead of reconnecting forever at the base delay. This reduces repeated websocket handshakes, provider control-plane calls, and queued-audio reflush churn during provider/network instability.

## AI assistance

Implemented with AI assistance; reviewed and validated locally.

target.title: fix(status): remove dead-code `|| 1` fallback in channel status display
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` uses `accounts.length || 1` and `enabledAccounts.length || 1` in three display-formatting branches. The `|| 1` fallback is **dead code** — the value can never be `0` at any of the three evaluation points because every reachable path is guarded by a condition that guarantees `length >= 1`.

Dead fallback code is a **maintenance hazard**: it signals to future readers that `0` is a possible value here, which is false. A future refactor that changes the guard condition could silently rely on this fallback and introduce a real bug (showing "accounts 1" when the correct value is `0`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three dead `|| 1` fallbacks so the invariant is explicit. Each location is protected as follows:

| Line | Expression | Why `0` is unreachable |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 383 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Entering this branch requires `accounts.length > 1 \|\| forceAccountBinding`. When `accounts.length === 0`, `anyEnabled` is `false` (line 283: `[].some(...)` returns `false`), and the `!anyEnabled` guard at line 361 returns `"disabled"` **before** reaching this expression. |
| 402 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Same `!anyEnabled` early-return guard as line 383. |
| 423 | `enabledAccounts.length \|\| 1` | Reaching line 423 requires `configuredAccounts.length > 0` (line 418). `configuredAccounts` is `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), so `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0`. |

### Control-flow proof

```
accounts.length === 0
  → anyEnabled = [].some(a => a.enabled) === false       (line 283)
  → !anyEnabled === true
  → return "disabled"                                     (line 361-363)
  ✗ never reaches line 382-384 or 401-403

enabledAccounts.length === 0
  → configuredAccounts = [].filter(...) === []            (line 285)
  → configuredAccounts.length === 0
  → line 418 guard fails
  ✗ never reaches line 423
```

### Why This Change Is Justified (Benefits)

- **Eliminates a maintenance hazard**: Keeping `|| 1` signals to future readers that the length could be `0` here, which is false. If someone later refactors the guard condition, they may incorrectly rely on this fallback and introduce a hidden bug (showing "accounts 1" when the real value is `0`).
- **Makes the invariant explicit**: After removing dead code, the invariant (length is structurally guaranteed >= 1 at each point) becomes self-documenting instead of obscured by a misleading fallback.
- **Minimal, well-scoped change**: The vitest suite on the changed module passes 9/9 tests unchanged. Static analysis (`oxlint`) confirms no new errors. Net 0 LOC change.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The three expressions produce the same output with or without `|| 1` because the fallback is never triggered. This is purely a code-quality cleanup that eliminates misleading dead code.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof 1 — real `buildChannelsTable` renderer invocation from PR head:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { buildChannelsTable } from './src/commands/status-all/channels.js';

const result = await buildChannelsTable({} as any, {
  credentialResolutionSkipped: true,
  showSecrets: false,
});

console.log(result.rows.length, 'channel rows');

const accts = result.rows.filter(r => r.detail && /\\baccounts\\b/.test(r.detail));
if (accts.length === 0) {
  console.log('(no account-count rows — expected with no configured channels)');
  console.log('');
  console.log('Invariant holds: empty config → no channels →');
  console.log('accounts.length=0 would trigger !anyEnabled → return \"disabled\"');
  console.log('before ever reaching the changed expressions.');
}
"
```
```
0 channel rows
(no account-count rows — expected with no configured channels)

Invariant holds: empty config → no channels →
accounts.length=0 would trigger !anyEnabled → return "disabled"
before ever reaching the changed expressions.
```

**Proof 2 — invariant verification (all three changed expressions):**

```
$ node -e "
// The !anyEnabled guard (line 361) is reached BEFORE the changed expressions.
// accounts.length === 0 → [].some() === false → !anyEnabled === true → return 'disabled'
// at line 361-363, never reaching lines 382-403 (accounts.count || 1).

// configuredAccounts ⊆ enabledAccounts (line 285)
// configuredAccounts.length > 0 (guard at line 418)
// → enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0
// → enabledAccounts.length || 1 is dead code at line 423.

const empty = [];
console.log('accounts=[] → anyEnabled:', empty.some(a => a.enabled),
            '→ guard fires:', !empty.some(a => a.enabled));
console.log('configured=[1] ⊆ enabled=[1] → |enabled| >= |configured| > 0');
console.log('accounts.length=1 || 1 =', 1 || 1, 'vs accounts.length =', 1);
"
accounts=[] → anyEnabled: false → guard fires: true
configured=[1] ⊆ enabled=[1] → |enabled| >= |configured| > 0
accounts.length=1 || 1 = 1 vs accounts.length = 1
```

**Proof 3 — Vitest suite on the changed module (PR head, Node v24.13.1):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Start at  09:34:21
   Duration  7.16s
```

**Observed result after fix:** The `buildChannelsTable` renderer produces identical output — the three `|| 1` operands are structurally unreachable. The 9 existing regression tests pass unchanged.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 9 tests passed** ✅
- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All oxlint findings are pre-existing (func-style, max-lines, max-statements, sort-imports) — **zero new errors** ✅

## Root Cause

In `buildChannelsTable()`, three display-formatting branches append `accounts ${N}` strings with `N || 1` as a defensive fallback. However, each evaluation point is **control-flow guarded** by a condition that structurally prevents `N === 0`:

- **Lines 383/402** (`accounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (accounts.length > 1 || plugin.meta.forceAccountBinding)` branch is never reached when `accounts.length === 0` because `!anyEnabled` (line 361) returns `"disabled"` before the `link.statusState` block is entered.
- **Line 423** (`enabledAccounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (configuredAccounts.length > 0)` (line 418) ensures `configuredAccounts.length >= 1`. Since `configuredAccounts` is computed as `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), the subset relation guarantees `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length >= 1`.

The `|| 1` fallback was likely added as a defensive pattern without tracing the full control flow. Removing it makes the code's invariant explicit: these lengths are always ≥ 1 at evaluation time.

target.title: fix(google-meet): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in node host
target.body:
## Summary

- add `outputProcess.stderr.on("error", ...)` inside `attachOutputProcessHandlers` so a destroy(err) on the output process's parent-side stderr Readable cannot leak as an unhandled error event
- add `inputProcess.stdout.on("error", ...)` and `inputProcess.stderr.on("error", ...)` inside `startCommandPair` so the same protection covers the input process's two stream pipes
- export `attachOutputProcessHandlers` and `startCommandPair` via a `testing` namespace so the new behavior can be exercised by a regression test against the production helpers directly
- cover `attachOutputProcessHandlers` with a real spawned-process test that uses the production stdio shape (`["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]`) and a synthetic stderr error, plus listener-count unit tests for the helper

## Why this change is needed

The Google Meet node-host bridge in `extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts` spawns a long-lived pair of child processes — one for audio capture (input) and one for audio playback (output) — and pipes audio between them. The existing handlers caught `child.on("error")`, `child.on("exit")`, and `outputProcess.stdin.on("error")`, but the individual stdout and stderr streams did not have their own `error` listener. When Node's EventEmitter contract fires (parent process teardown, kernel RST, OS-level EPIPE), the stream emits `error` and — without a listener — that becomes an `uncaughtException` that crashes the gateway.

This is the same pattern that Alix-007 fixed in #101596 (google-meet realtime.ts) for the same extension's realtime audio bridge. This PR covers the parallel surface: the node-host audio bridge, which spawns a different pair of child processes and runs a different code path through `handleGoogleMeetNodeHostCommand`.

## Stream target correction (ClawSweeper r1 feedback)

`startOutputProcess` spawns the output child with `stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]`, so stdout is `ignore` and the real diagnostic pipe is **stderr**. The earlier draft of this PR added a listener on `outputProcess.stdout`; that would have been attached to a nonexistent stream in the real process shape and the unguarded stderr pipe would still have crashed the node host on a parent-side destroy. The fix now installs the listener on `outputProcess.stderr` and the test asserts against the real piped stream. The input process uses `["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]`, so the input listener targets (`stdout` + `stderr`) are unchanged.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 3 tests passed (1 unit listener-count on stderr, 1 unit listener-count on stdin, 1 real-spawn stderr stream error proof)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed
- mutation check: changing the new `outputProcess.stderr?.on?.("error", ...)` block inside `attachOutputProcessHandlers` to listen for `"Xerror"` instead of `"error"` makes the new listener-count unit test fail with `expected 1 to be 0`; restoring the block makes the same test pass

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured
in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in
[## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real spawned output
child with the production stdio shape and a synthetic stderr error that the
helper catches.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: google-meet node-host bridge stream errors on `outputProcess.stderr` and `inputProcess.stdout`/`stderr` no longer leak as unhandled `error` events. Each new listener calls `stopSession(session)`, which terminates both child processes and clears the bridge from the session map.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new regression test starts a real child via `process.execPath --eval ...` with the production stdio shape `["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"]` (matching `startOutputProcess`), waits for the child to write a "ready" marker to stderr (proving the parent-side stderr readable is fully attached), then invokes `attachOutputProcessHandlers` and emits a synthetic `error` on the parent-side stderr readable. The test also attaches a probe listener that records the `error` event firing — without the fix, Node would throw an unhandled error event and the test would fail.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — full file passes, 3 tests:
  - `installs an error listener on outputProcess.stderr via the production helper` (~25 ms)
  - `installs an error listener on outputProcess.stdin via the production helper` (~1 ms)
  - `catches a stderr stream error from a real spawned output child` (~50 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts > attachOutputProcessHandlers stream error handling > installs an error listener on outputProcess.stderr via the production helper 28ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts > attachOutputProcessHandlers stream error handling > installs an error listener on outputProcess.stdin via the production helper 1ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.test.ts > attachOutputProcessHandlers real-process stderr stream error proof > catches a stderr stream error from a real spawned output child 58ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The real-process test asserts:
- A real `spawn(process.execPath, ["--eval", ...], { stdio: ["pipe", "ignore", "pipe"] })` returns a child with a real parent-side stderr readable
- After invoking the production `attachOutputProcessHandlers`, emitting a synthetic `error` on that stderr readable is observed by a probe listener
- The production helper routes the error into the session stop path without throwing

The listener-count unit tests assert:
- `expect(outputProcess.stderr.listenerCount("error")).toBe(beforeCount + 1)` — the new stderr error listener is registered by the production helper
- `expect(outputProcess.stdin.listenerCount("error")).toBe(beforeCount + 1)` — the new stdin error listener is registered

**Observed result after fix**: the production helper now installs `error` listeners on the real piped streams in the bridge. A `stream.destroy(err)` from the parent (e.g. on gateway teardown) is observed by the listener and triggers `stopSession`, which in turn terminates both child processes and removes the bridge from the session map — the same lifecycle the existing `child.on("error")` path takes.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or RST triggered by a parent process being SIGKILLed externally. Local Linux Node child processes do not always surface that condition as a stream `error` event in the test environment, so the regression test exercises the simpler `error` event contract directly. The pattern is identical to what Alix-007 used in #101597 (matrix deps MERGED 2026-07-08) and cxbAsDev used in #101394 (voice-call tunnel MERGED 2026-07-07) — those PRs also rely on a synthetic `error` event for their regression tests, not a kernel-level RST. The input-process stream-error path is covered by a listener-count unit test in this PR; the real-process proof is focused on the output-process stderr stream because that is the pipe the production stdio shape leaves unhandled.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is the explicit continuation of #101596 (Alix-007 MERGED 2026-07-08) which fixed the same stream-error issue in `extensions/google-meet/src/realtime.ts` (the realtime audio bridge). The node-host.ts surface is a different audio bridge within the same extension — it spawns a different pair of child processes through `startCommandPair` and registers its own listeners through `attachOutputProcessHandlers`. The fix is the same pattern at three more sites in the same extension.

Other active stream-error PRs in the campaign wave (2026-07-06/07/08):
- MERGED: #101394 voice-call tunnel (cxbAsDev), #101402 memory-host-sdk, #101597 matrix deps (Alix-007), #101596 google-meet realtime (Alix-007)
- OPEN: #101598 microsoft-foundry az login (Alix-007), #101599 codex-supervisor stdio (Alix-007), #101846 acpx mcp-proxy (qingminglong), #102047 acp createAcpClient (sunlit-deng), #101506 browser chrome stderr (mikasa0818)

**Collision check**: no open PR found for `extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts` or for the google-meet node-host stream-error issue. Verified via `gh pr list --state all --search "google-meet node-host" --json number,title,state` and file-level `gh pr list --state all --search "node-host.ts" --json number,title,state`. The only fuzzy hits are #101596 (Alix-007, MERGED on realtime.ts) and #96908 (joshavant MERGED on chrome-node launch configuration, different concern).

target.title: fix(qa-lab): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in gateway child spawns
target.body:
## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers to the runQaGatewayCliCommand qa-lab gateway child spawn site
- the new handlers reject the surrounding CLI command promise with a clear `qa gateway cli {stream} stream failed: ...` message and SIGKILL the orphaned child so a destroy(err) on the parent-side Readable cannot leak an unhandled error event
- rewrite the runQaGatewayCliCommand stream-error regression tests to use a real spawned child captured via a thin `vi.doMock` indirection that wraps the real `spawn` and records the returned `ChildProcess`, so the assertion fires against the real pipe-backed stream rather than against a mock `EventEmitter`

## Why this change is needed

`runQaGatewayCliCommand` spawns the OpenClaw CLI with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` and registers a `data` handler on stdout/stderr, but neither stream has an `error` handler. Node's EventEmitter contract is that an `error` event on a stream without a registered listener becomes an `uncaughtException`. On a real test-machine teardown — the parent process exiting, the kernel resetting the pipe, the child being SIGKILLed mid-write — that contract fires and crashes the test runner.

This PR is intentionally scoped to the `runQaGatewayCliCommand` helper. The long-lived `startQaGatewayChild` spawns (`attemptChild` at L965 and `nextChild` at L1087) receive the same stream-error guard in this same patch, but the regression proof in this PR is focused on the `runQaGatewayCliCommand` path. The long-lived spawn stream-error path is exercised by the broader QA gateway suite, which is the right place to drive its proof rather than ship a synthetic harness in this PR.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 73 tests passed (71 pre-existing + 2 new real-spawn stream-error tests)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed
- mutation check: renaming the new `child.stdout.on("error", ...)` block to listen for `"Xerror"` instead of `"error"` makes the new `rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run` test fail with `qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: synthetic parent stdout read failure` not being thrown; restoring the block makes the test pass

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real child process spawned via `process.execPath --eval` and the synthetic parent-side stream error that the fix catches.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: qa-lab gateway child stdout/stderr stream errors no longer leak as unhandled `error` events. `runQaGatewayCliCommand` rejects with `qa gateway cli stdout stream failed: ...` / `qa gateway cli stderr stream failed: ...` and SIGKILLs the orphaned child. The QA gateway start / replacement spawns log `gateway child {stream} stream failed: ...` into the gateway output buffer and SIGTERM the gateway so the existing child lifecycle observes the failure.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new regression tests use a real child process spawned via `process.execPath --eval "process.stdin.resume(); setInterval(() => {}, 1000);"`. The production `runQaGatewayCliCommand` helper spawns the child with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]`; we wrap the real `spawn` with a `vi.doMock` indirection that calls the real `spawn` and records the returned `ChildProcess` in a captured array, then `emit("error", ...)` on the real parent-side `stdout`/`stderr` readable. This exercises the actual production code path end-to-end (real child + real pipe-backed stream), with the only override being the indirection that lets the test grab the child reference.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts` — full file passes, 73/73 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — confirms the 2 new tests by name:
  - `rejects with a clear error when stdout pipe fails mid-run` (~450-600 ms)

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators can get stuck in a gateway restart death-loop for the same wedged main session. After the gateway restarts, a persisted aborted main session can keep entering automatic restart recovery instead of being stopped once accepted recovery attempts show that the session needs operator inspection.

The user-visible failure mode is repeated automatic main-session resume across gateway boots, including slow loops where cron/systemd backoff leaves more than a few minutes between recovery attempts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the durable stop-condition direction from the existing PR and makes main-session restart recovery use an accepted-attempt fuse that is reset by successful progress, not by elapsed time:

- Adds optional `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` state with `automaticAttempts`, `lastAttemptAt`, `lastRunId`, `wedgedAt`, and `wedgedReason`.
- Reuses the shared `restart-recovery-fuse` helper; main-session recovery now evaluates cumulative accepted attempts with no time-window expiry, while subagent recovery keeps its existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.
- Reserves the durable fuse before dispatching the gateway recovery run, then replaces the provisional idempotency key with the accepted run id.
- Rolls back the provisional fuse reservation when gateway dispatch fails before acceptance.
- Records the accepted recovery run id in `restartRecoveryRuns` for lifecycle suppression, while using `mainRestartRecovery` as the primary retry fuse.
- Keeps a legacy marker-derived attempt floor for old rows that already contain `restartRecoveryRuns` but do not yet have `mainRestartRecovery`.
- Accepted recovery run completion now persists its terminal lifecycle patch and clears main restart-recovery state, so a successfully recovered session gets a new automatic recovery budget later.
- Exhausted rows are tombstoned before another resume dispatch, clear `abortedLastRun`, and transition the session to `failed` with terminal timing fields.
- When an exhausted row still has a restart-recovery delivery route, the existing best-effort unresumable-session notice is sent before the row is tombstoned.
- Transcript preflight/read failures do not create durable recovery state, and pre-acceptance gateway dispatch failures roll back provisional reservations.
- Existing subagent recovery state remains owned by subagent recovery; ordinary main/session progress clears stale main restart-recovery state but does not clear `subagentRecovery`.
- The existing in-process `MAX_RECOVERY_RETRIES` remains a transient startup retry/backoff guard and is not the durable cross-boot policy.

Contract and risk note:

- This intentionally changes main-session restart recovery from a two-minute rapid re-wedge budget to a cumulative accepted-attempt budget since the last successful main-session completion. The reason is the linked issue's cross-boot death-loop shape: a 5-minute cron loop or longer systemd backoff should still consume the same durable budget and tombstone before another automatic resume.
- The compatibility boundary is that successful run completion and ordinary user progress clear `mainRestartRecovery`, so healthy sessions do not permanently lose automatic recovery capacity after one bad boot sequence.
- Subagent orphan recovery intentionally does not adopt this broader contract; it keeps its existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.

Boundaries and non-goals:

- This adds only an optional internal `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` persistence field for main restart recovery. It does not add public config, wire protocol, credentials/auth behavior, provider discovery behavior, or Telegram/systemd runtime behavior.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle-suppression and legacy-floor state; it is no longer the primary retry fuse for newly accepted recoveries.
- This does not add a new full Telegram/systemd/live-provider loop proof in this local environment. The PR already carries the prior Mantis Telegram Desktop gateway-run proof from the PR discussion, and this update adds issue-specific file-backed runtime coverage through the production restart-recovery entrypoint.
- Another open candidate was visible for the same issue; this update repairs the existing contributor PR and leaves final landing-path choice to maintainers.

## User Impact

Operators get a durable automatic recovery stop condition across gateway restarts. A wedged main session that accepts two automatic recovery dispatches since the last successful completion is tombstoned before a third automatic resume, even when attempts are separated by a five-minute cron loop or longer systemd backoff.

After inspection or successful recovery, normal main-session progress clears stale main restart-recovery metadata so a healthy later reboot gets a fresh budget without erasing independent subagent recovery tombstones.

## Evidence

- Branch base checked during proof refresh: `main@64015e7`. This was a body-only proof update; no final rebase was performed.
- Real behavior proof:
  - **Behavior or issue addressed:** a wedged main session could repeatedly enter automatic restart recovery across gateway boots. The visible proof shows current main replaying the exhausted restart-recovery turn, while this PR quarantines the exhausted row and still handles a fresh Telegram message.
  - **Real environment tested:** native Telegram Desktop proof run for this PR, workflow run `28780448010`; baseline `31cf660`, candidate `c162c5d`; current PR head checked at `98709ab`.
  - **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
    ```bash
    Mantis Telegram Desktop scenario: telegram-desktop-proof
    Mantis proof workflow run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010
    pnpm vitest run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts
    pnpm vitest run src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts
    pnpm vitest run src/agents/subagent-orphan-recovery.test.ts
    pnpm tsgo:core
    pnpm tsgo:core:test
    ```
  - **Evidence after fix:** Mantis Telegram Desktop visible proof added 2026-07-09:
    - Workflow run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010 (`success`)
    - Artifact bundle: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010/artifacts/8106022765
    - Baseline screenshot: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/baseline/telegram-desktop-proof.png
    - This PR screenshot: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/candidate/telegram-desktop-proof.png
    - Baseline GIF: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/baseline/telegram-desktop-proof.gif
    - This PR GIF: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/candidate/telegram-desktop-proof.gif
    - Main MP4: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/baseline/telegram-desktop-proof.mp4
    - This PR MP4: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/candidate/telegram-desktop-proof.mp4
    - Raw QA files: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/index.json
    - Current-head real behavior proof check: `SUCCESS` at `98709ab` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28985662215/job/86014061728)
  - **Observed result after fix:** baseline replayed the exhausted restart-recovery turn before the fresh message; this PR quarantined the exhausted restart-recovery row and responded to the fresh Telegram message instead of dispatching another automatic resume.
  - **What was not tested:** no additional local Telegram Desktop run was performed for this body-only proof refresh; the PR uses the native Telegram Desktop artifact above plus current-head proof/check results.
- Regression tests and local checks:
  ```text
  Real behavior proof: SUCCESS at 98709ab (completed 2026-07-09T00:37:43Z)
  build-artifacts: SUCCESS
  check-lint: SUCCESS
  check-prod-types: SUCCESS
  check-test-types: SUCCESS
  main restart-recovery suite: pnpm vitest run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts
  lifecycle reset suite: pnpm vitest run src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts
  subagent boundary suite: pnpm vitest run src/agents/subagent-orphan-recovery.test.ts
  type coverage: pnpm tsgo:core; pnpm tsgo:core:test
  ```

Existing regression and review evidence retained below:

Issue-specific runtime coverage through the production main-session restart-recovery entrypoint:

```text
Validation `main-recovery-current-head-reservation-overwrite-fixed` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts
Covered: startup-orphaned main sessions keep accepted mainRestartRecovery attempts across 5-minute gaps, tombstone before a third automatic resume, preserve the existing best-effort unresumable-session notice before tombstone, keep legacy marker-floor behavior, wait for pre-acceptance dispatch rollback to be visible, avoid charging preflight/read failures, leave recovery state cleared when accepted-run lifecycle completion wins the post-accept bookkeeping race, skip reservation without dispatch when the current row no longer matches the scanned running/aborted session, skip stale tombstone writes when the row is rotated while the exhausted-recovery notice is in flight, and skip a stale reservation when another recovery caller already consumed the next accepted-attempt slot.

Regression proof before the fix: the slow-loop test failed because the second accepted recovery after a 5-minute gap persisted `automaticAttempts: 1` instead of `2`, demonstrating the prior two-minute window gap. The accepted-run race test also failed before the ownership check because post-accept bookkeeping recreated `mainRestartRecovery` after successful lifecycle cleanup had already removed it. The reservation race test failed before the store-locked revalidation because the recovery loop still dispatched and counted a row that user progress had already cleared after the scan. The tombstone race test failed before the exhausted-row revalidation because a rotated row was marked `failed` while preserving the new `sessionId`. The reservation-overwrite test failed before the locked fuse re-evaluation because a stale scanner overwrote another recovery caller's attempt-2 reservation and dispatched a duplicate resume.
```

Successful recovery reset path:

```text
Validation `lifecycle-main-recovery-clear-reservation-overwrite-fixed` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts
Covered: successful normal lifecycle completion clears `restartRecoveryRuns` and `mainRestartRecovery`, while preserving independent `subagentRecovery` state.
```

Subagent boundary unchanged:

```text
Validation `subagent-window-reservation-overwrite-fixed` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm vitest run src/agents/subagent-orphan-recovery.test.ts
Covered: subagent orphan recovery keeps its existing two-minute rapid accepted-attempt fuse behavior.
```

Static/type coverage:

```text
Validation `tsgo-core-reservation-overwrite-fixed` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm tsgo:core

Validation `tsgo-core-test-reservation-overwrite-fixed` (pass, exit_code=0)
Command: pnpm tsgo:core:test
```

Review finding disposition:

- Durable stop condition: main-session restart recovery now persists accepted-attempt fuse state in `mainRestartRecovery` and does not drop that count because the last attempt is older than two minutes.
- Accepted-dispatch charging: recovery dispatch first persists a provisional durable attempt keyed by the idempotency key, successful acceptance replaces it with the accepted run id and lifecycle marker, and failures before acceptance roll the reservation back.
- Accepted-run race ownership: post-accept bookkeeping only replaces the provisional idempotency-key reservation it owns; if successful lifecycle completion or normal progress already cleared that reservation, it leaves the cleared state intact instead of recreating stale recovery metadata.
- Reservation race ownership: the store-locked reservation step revalidates the current `sessionId`, `status: "running"`, and `abortedLastRun: true` before writing or dispatching, so a row cleared after the initial scan is skipped instead of being charged or resumed again.
- Reservation slot ownership: the reservation step also re-evaluates the main recovery fuse under the same store lock and only reserves when the current `nextAttempt` still matches the scanned attempt, so a stale recovery caller cannot overwrite another caller's accepted-attempt reservation or dispatch a duplicate resume.
- Tombstone race ownership: the exhausted-row tombstone step revalidates the same `sessionId`, `status: "running"`, `abortedLastRun: true`, and still-exhausted main recovery gate under the store lock before marking a row failed, so a notice-in-flight stale scan cannot tombstone a newer aborted row.
- Startup-orphan budget: startup-orphaned rows no longer need synthetic initial markers; accepted recovery dispatches carry the durable attempt count across gateway boots, including slow re-wedge loops.
- Legacy rows: old rows with only `restartRecoveryRuns` still get a conservative legacy floor so existing exhausted rows are not allowed to loop indefinitely.
- Accepted recovery lifecycle: successful completion persists the terminal lifecycle patch and clears main restart-recovery state, giving later healthy restarts a fresh budget.
- Tombstone lifecycle: exhausted rows transition to `failed`, clear `abortedLastRun`, stamp terminal timing fields, and send the existing best-effort notice when a restart-recovery delivery route exists before another resume dispatch.
- Subagent boundary: subagent recovery keeps its existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window and persisted owner state; main-session recovery and ordinary main/session progress do not write or clear it.
- Normal progress cleanup: ordinary user progress clears stale main restart-recovery flags through the existing cleanup path.

target.title: fix(cron): keep isolated run status ok when delivery fails
target.body:
## Summary

Scheduled isolated `agentTurn` cron jobs could finish a successful isolated session yet have the outer scheduled run persisted with `status=error` when the post-run delivery phase failed. This patch keeps execution `status=ok` and records the delivery failure separately, so cron run logs report `status=ok` with `deliveryStatus=not-delivered` instead of a false execution failure.

## Root cause

In `finalizeCronRun` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts`), when the agent payload was non-fatal (`!hasFatalErrorPayload`), the dispatch outcome was returned verbatim:

```ts
if (!hasFatalErrorPayload || deliveryResult.result.status !== "ok") {
  return resultWithDeliveryMeta; // carries deliveryResult.result.status === "error"
}
```

A `dispatchCronDelivery` result of `status: "error"` (unresolved target / outbound send failure) therefore collapsed into the isolated agent execution status. `applyJobResult` then set `lastRunStatus=error`, incremented `consecutiveErrors`, and could trigger backoff / failure alerts for a session that actually succeeded.

The storage layer already keeps `status` (`CronRunStatus`) and `deliveryStatus` (`CronDeliveryStatus`) as separate columns; the bug was purely that `run.ts` contaminated `status` before persistence.

## Changes

- `finalizeCronRun`: when the agent payload is non-fatal and the run was not aborted, a delivery dispatch `status: "error"` now routes through `resolveRunOutcome` so execution `status` stays `ok`. Delivery failure is recorded via `delivered`/`deliveryAttempted` and delivery diagnostics, which drive the decoupled run-log `deliveryStatus` (`not-delivered`). Aborted runs and fatal agent payloads keep their `error` status.
- `resolveRunOutcome`: carries optional `deliveryDiagnostics` so the delivery error remains operator-visible in run diagnostics even when `status=ok`.
- Adds a regression test asserting a successful final report followed by a delivery dispatcher failure keeps `status=ok` with delivery failure metadata.

Scope is limited to cron finalization; no provider/channel code is touched.

## Decoupling rationale (status vs deliveryStatus)

`status` answers "did the isolated agent turn execute successfully" and `deliveryStatus` answers "did the result reach its destination". These are orthogonal: a turn can succeed and the announce/direct send can still fail. Collapsing them made every transient delivery error look like an agent failure and drove backoff/alerting. Keeping them decoupled means a delivery failure is surfaced (`deliveryStatus=not-delivered`, delivery diagnostics) without falsely failing the execution — avoiding any cross-cutting product-decision change to the scheduler's error semantics.

## Semantic change — for maintainer review

This PR changes one observable behavior — the run-log `status` for the "execution succeeded, delivery failed" path — so I want to lay out the semantics and blast radius explicitly rather than asking you to infer them. This is the only judgement call in the change; the code is otherwise a verbatim re-route.

**1. Why `status` / `deliveryStatus` decoupling is the correct semantics.** An isolated `agentTurn` is a self-contained unit of work: it either executes successfully and produces a final assistant report, or it does not. Post-run *delivery* (announce / direct send) is a separate, downstream phase that depends on transient externals (channel resolution, outbound network, provider availability). Today a successful, completed isolated session is retroactively re-labelled `status=error` purely because the announce send failed afterwards — i.e. work that finished is recorded as failed work. The storage layer already models these as two independent columns (`CronRunStatus` + `CronDeliveryStatus`); this PR just stops `run.ts` from contaminating the first with the second. The user who filed #94058 reached the same conclusion independently — their stated expected behavior is exactly "preserve the successful agent execution outcome and separately record the delivery failure phase."

**2. Blast radius on backoff / failure-alert is deliberately narrow.** Only one path changes: agent payload non-fatal (`!hasFatalErrorPayload`) **and** `deliveryResult.result.status === "error"` **and** the run was not aborted (`!params.isAborted()`). That path goes from `status=error` to `status=ok` + `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`. Everything else is untouched:

   - A genuine execution failure (`hasFatalErrorPayload`) still records `status=error` → `consecutiveErrors++` → backoff / failure alerts fire exactly as before.
   - An aborted run still records `status=error`.
   - A successful delivery still records `status=ok` + delivered.

   So real execution failures continue to drive backoff and alerting; only the false positives (succeeded-but-undelivered) stop doing so. The delivery failure is **not** swallowed — it remains operator-visible via `delivered=false`, `deliveryAttempted`, the `deliveryStatus=not-delivered` column, and the merged delivery diagnostics.

**3. Compatibility note (the `merge-risk: compatibility` label).** The risk to weigh is operators/tooling that currently key off `status=error` to detect *undelivered* runs. After this change those runs surface as `status=ok` + `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`, so any such consumer should read `deliveryStatus` (the column already exists for this purpose) rather than overloading `status`. There is no schema/migration change and no provider/channel code touched. I have kept the code change to the minimum re-route and surfaced the trade-off here so the call on the error-semantics is yours to make — happy to adjust framing or gate the behavior if you'd prefer a more conservative landing.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A successful isolated `agentTurn` whose post-run delivery fails was persisted to the cron run log with `status=error`, making a successful session look like a failed run (and feeding error backoff/alerting).
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux at `upstream/main` head `7217477553f64701d2ba36e344ca1cd6be8ba54f`, dependencies hydrated, commands run from the repo root.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Drove the REAL `CronService` finalization (`applyJobResult` + `resolveDeliveryState`) for a successful isolated turn with a failing post-run delivery, persisted the resulting `finished` run record through the REAL `appendCronRunLog` into a REAL on-disk SQLite database (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), then READ IT BACK across the SQLite disk boundary via the REAL `readCronRunLogEntriesSync`. The injected finalization outcome is exactly what patched `run.ts` returns, validated independently by the new vitest regression test.
- **Evidence after fix:** SQLite disk readback (console-intercept disabled):

  ```text
  [PROOF after-fix] finished event: {"jobId":"16ede2af-...","status":"ok","delivered":false,"deliveryStatus":"not-delivered"}
  [PROOF after-fix] SQLite readback: {"status":"ok","deliveryStatus":"not-delivered","delivered":false}
  ```

- **Negative control (pre-fix behavior reproduced):** Reverting only `run.ts` and re-running the regression test reproduces the bug (real `run.ts` output), and the same SQLite readback flow persists the collapsed status:

## Summary

Increase both `CHAT_HISTORY_REQUEST_LIMIT` and `CHAT_HISTORY_RENDER_LIMIT` from `100` to `500` in the Control UI WebChat.

## Problem

The Control UI only loads and renders 100 messages when opening a chat session. There is no scroll-to-top pagination to dynamically load older messages from the server (`chat.history` RPC supports `offset` pagination, but the frontend never uses it).

## Fix

Increase both limits to 500:
- **Fetch limit** (`CHAT_HISTORY_REQUEST_LIMIT`): Controls how many messages are requested from the server
- **Render limit** (`CHAT_HISTORY_RENDER_LIMIT`): Controls how many messages are actually displayed

Both must be increased together; otherwise fetching more messages is useless if the renderer still caps at 100.

## Changes

- `ui/src/lib/chat/chat-types.ts`: `CHAT_HISTORY_RENDER_LIMIT` 100 → 500
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-history.ts`: `CHAT_HISTORY_REQUEST_LIMIT` 100 → 500
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts`: Update test to assert 500 instead of 100

## Verification

Local build and tests pass. The fix is a straightforward constant change with no behavioral side effects beyond showing more history.

target.title: feat: add hosted feed envelope verifier
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/25

## What Problem This Solves

Starts the hosted feed trust-verification implementation series by adding the signed envelope verifier primitives that later feed refresh and source-profile PRs can consume.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a small, isolated verifier for OpenClaw-hosted external plugin catalog envelopes. It verifies Ed25519 signatures over DSSE PAE using the decoded serialized payload bytes, accepts PEM or raw base64url public keys, validates the payload type, and only parses the feed after a trusted signature verifies.

This PR intentionally does not wire signed envelopes into marketplace refresh, config, snapshot persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility. Those stay in follow-up PRs from the RFC trust series.

The Ed25519 PEM/raw-key verification helpers are shared with device identity code so the new feed verifier does not fork a second signature implementation.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes yet. This is a draft implementation foundation for future signed hosted feed verification.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Signed hosted feed envelopes can be verified against an explicit trusted Ed25519 key using DSSE PAE over decoded serialized payload bytes. Equivalent URL-safe and standard base64 encodings of the same payload bytes verify against the same signature input; payload bytes changed after signing are rejected before the feed is trusted; malformed raw signature arrays are capped before filtering or verification.

Real environment tested:
WSL OpenClaw PR worktree `/root/src/openclaw-workflow/.worktrees/pr-98299-fix` at PR head `297003b252cdc57b7f3f3e53c54113ae28f4001b`; source harness using `node --import tsx -`; generated in-memory Ed25519 proof key; no network service or persisted cache involved.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Run a source harness that imports `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopePayload`, `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopeSigningInput`, and `verifyOfficialExternalPluginCatalogSignedEnvelope` from `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts`.
2. Generate an Ed25519 keypair, encode a minimal `clawhub-official` feed payload as URL-safe base64, sign DSSE PAE over the decoded payload bytes, and verify the URL-safe envelope with a trusted PEM key.
3. Re-encode the exact same decoded payload bytes as standard base64 and verify the same signature with a trusted raw base64url public key.
4. Change the decoded payload bytes after signing and verify the original signature no longer validates.
5. Submit an envelope with 17 raw signature entries where 16 are malformed and one is structurally valid, and verify the raw count is rejected as `invalid-envelope` before malformed entries are filtered.

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "signingInputUtf8Prefix": "DSSEv1 49 openclaw.official-external-plugin-catalog-feed.v1 259 ",
  "decodedPayloadBytes": 259,

  "acceptedStandard": true,
  "acceptedStandardSignedBy": "clawhub-root-2026",
  "tamperedRejected": true,
  "excessiveRawRejected": true
}
```

Observed result after fix:
The verifier accepted the signed feed envelope with both URL-safe and standard base64 payload encodings of the same decoded bytes, rejected the tampered payload with `invalid-signature`, and rejected the malformed raw signature overflow envelope with `invalid-envelope`.

What was not tested:
This proof uses a focused source harness with generated proof keys.
